Blanca, how we wanted you to be magnificent! Instead, you were middling. We have been wanting to come for some time; this time last year, we had an absolutely phenomenal tasting menu at Brooklyn Fare. Admittedly, it frames my expectations.

There were some real standouts (broth-based dishes, pasta dishes, the bread and butter), but overall the menu did not meet expectations and was quite frankly lacking in courses to the tune of about 5.  

Moreover, the wine pairing was delicious though incredibly sparing, to be kind. The reason, according to the sommelier, is that it's a "tasting" and "people... don't always know about wines... and have gotten really drunk." 

I am disappointed at the consistency of Blanca and the service. Condescension has no place at the table at Blanca. Cesar Ramirez and company set the bar... and allow you to properly sit at the bar.

I was looking forward to my first experience at this much-acclaimed restaurant... Only to be disappointed. 

Sure, food is very good. But at this price point, the Brooklyn Fare is a much better choice - where all the plates are going to blow your mind away. Instead, at Blanca, everything is well executed but there are maybe only 4 or 5 plates that are really worth the detour... 

Wine pairing... why not, I found that the previous comments on the quantity were not that deserved... or maybe they took them into account ? 

Overall, good restaurant for sure, but I won't be back. Hence the 3 stars.

I did not read the reviews prior to our visit since I didn't want any element of the meal ruined.  I should have since if I had, I would have skipped this restaurant.  This restaurant is overhyped.

The restaurant is very casual and has comfortable seats in a horse shoe setting that faces the kitchen.  Unlike Atera where the execution is like a ballet, the service is haphazard.  These are not 5 star servers.  One server was so hard to understand that many times, I had to ask another server what I was eating since there are no menus.  

We had no idea at the start of the meal what we would be eating, how many courses or anything about our meal.  Our Amex confirm said we were going to have 28 courses but our server told us we had 21.  That might explain why were were still hungry at the end of the meal.  I have NEVER left any tasting dinner hungry.  In fact, I usually, cannot finish and end up taking the petit fours home.  We actually, considered purchasing a pizza from Robertas to eat on the train home and settled on a mediocre cinnamon roll instead.  The server at Robertas told us many people leave hungry.  That is UNACCEPTABLE for a meal that cost $500 with no alcohol but included tax and tip for two.  

The worst part was since we faced the kitchen, we could see the extra duck, lamb and beef and wondered if they were holding back on us so the staff could have the leftovers.  We even tried joking and asked for more.  We were not joking.  We were hungry.  There was a noticeable difference between the portion size on some plates.    

We were also told that the meal was never repeated and photos were not permitted.  The meal is apparently, repeated since the diner on 2/6/14 had our exact meal and there are photos on yelp.  

The food was good but it in no way compares to Alinea or any of the other top tier restaurant in NYC or elsewhere.  Some courses were exceptional but others were just okay.  I am not sure when bread became a course but thank goodness or I would have needed the pizza.  The bread actually, felt like filler.  

The three courses of ice-cream, sorbet and palate cleanser was a bit redundant.  Yet, there was no real dessert other than the ice creams and the equivalent of petite fours which were two marshmallows and one chocolate.  The house cured proscuitto was so fatty as was much of the meat.  The ravioli and the culantro ice cream were outstanding.  My daughter loved the fish plate.

The plating was nice but nothing that would cause me to want to take a photo if they even permitted it.  There was no magic in the plating.

But the crowning annoyance besides being hungry and btw, we are both thin women, was they forgot the birthday candle in my petite four which was apparently, the dessert.  The server's reaction was "bummer."  Really?  Another guest sitting next to me who was also celebrating her birthday, offered to share her candle.  My daughter asked another server who brought out an additional marshmallow and chocolate with a candle.  The food is apparently, rationed or we were eating their dinner.

I would not recommend this restaurant.  If you want a fabulous experience, go to Eleven Madison Park or Atera.  You will not be hungry and you will leave in awe.

Food was pretty good, and enjoyed the diversity of the food.  Two issues I had though:
1) I caught food poisoning the night before, and when I tried to cancel / move it, they immediately said they were charging me the full $400ish.  I understand there is a cancellation policy, but it seemed reasonable given the situation.  Since I was paying anyway, I went, was quasi-miserable the whole time, and hopefully didn't get people sick!
2) while the food is good, I don't think it justifies that high of price point.

I took my wife here for her 30th birthday.  It was tough to get a reservation, but I managed to do so on a weekend night and in time for the occasion.

The service was excellent.  The staff moves quickly through an array of (I'm guessing) 20 distinct courses.  There is an optional wine pairing, but to get the most out of the meal I opted out and my wife opted in.  I noted that one of their wine selections was particularly excellent, and when I emailed a few days later in order to get more information, they were happy to provide me with the vineyard and vintage at my request.

The meal was excellent in all respects.  I had a shrimp with an almost glass-like clarity that was more tender than anything I had ever had.  There were a couple of misses, but they were just dishes that were uninspired more than poor.

I do not recommend this place unless you have the money to blow though - it is about a third of a nice 1 bedroom in the same neighborhood.  That being said, this is a great place to go for two people for a special occasion.

Blanca was far and away the best meal I have ever had.  When I first moved to NYC my husband and I used to do tasting menus more often - we went to Babbo, Le Bernadin, WD-50, Momofuku Ko, Annisa, etc.  And then we stopped doing the tasting menu thing and started dining a la carte because we found ourselves generally more fulfilled (and often less stuffed) that way.  I think with every single tasting menu we did there was at least one course I wish I could have traded out for another dish that I really wanted to try.  We also found it to be so much harder to fully appreciate each course and remember what you ate in a tasting menu (particularly when you added in the wine pairing) because everything blurred together.

But Blanca might have rejuvenated my interest in the tasting menu approach because everything was just so freaking amazing.  I'm not going to describe each each course we had (or the wine that the sommelier paired with it), but I can say this - the meal did not disappoint in any way shape or form.  What I really loved was how distinct and perfectly prepared each course was - each ingredient was highlighted and every single component on a dish had a purpose and added to the dish.  I couldn't put a finger on any one type of cuisine or dominating influence - some dishes skewed Nordic (like the pickled cauliflower and shaved mackerel dish), others were Italian (pancetta), others were total melting pots.

My favorite ten courses out of the twenty or so courses we had are below:

- pancetta, cured in-house (the silkiest, most divinely porky thing I have ever tasted)
- Wagyu beef with trout lily leaf, kaffir lime yogurt and horseradish (amazing texture and taste - this was one of those dishes where every single component really worked together to give you a really wonderful dish)
- sunchoke purée with honeycomb, sea lettuce and nasturtium (beautiful and interesting)
- eggplant ceviche with burnt eggplant puree (the eggplant was so bright and delicious - not at all heavy and dull)
- plankton agnolotti (sounds totally bizarre, but it was divine - perfectly cooked and tender pasta with a salty filling, kissed with evoo)
- 'nduja ravioli (spicy sausage ravioli in a browned butter sauce - yum)
- salt roasted Japanese sweet potatoes with watercress juice, macadamia milk and espresso (the crispy crust on the sweet potatoes is something I would love to be able to duplicate at home, but I know I am not that cool and I don't know how you get the idea to combine watercress juice, macadamia milk and espresso with sweet potatoes, but it was very interesting and tasty)
- deep sea perch with black lime and egg yolk (slightly creamy from the egg and super funky from the black lime)
- duck breast, kumquat, beet mole sauce (beautifully cooked duck with a really interesting sauce)
- lamb with mint jelly, fava leaf and soy salt (amazing - I totally loved this dish)

I should also mention the bread course (Hawaiian roll - made with pineapple juice and lava salt, buckwheat bread with nuts and something else and really lovely butter) and the palate cleanser (lemon fro-yo with ginger juice and cucumbers).  Both of those "courses" were amazing.  I generally don't find bread courses or palate cleansers to be that memorable, but they were so wonderful.

I would highly recommend Blanca to anyone who wants to indulge themselves in a really fantastic meal in a far more low key setting than most restaurants that serve this caliber of food.  Also (and this is a matter of personal opinion) this is the first tasting menu I walked out of feeling the perfect balance of being full (but not stuffed) and tipsy (but not too drunk to remember the final courses of the meal).

Second visit to Blanca.  Was glad to see that after eating here two months ago, many of the dishes had changed and some of my favorites, like the plankton agnolotti,  stayed.  Although the cilantro sorbet wasn't my favorite the last time, I enjoyed it with the black rice "soup" this time.  Tip:  DO NOT arrive late!  When they say they will start serving at 5pm, they mean it.  A couple arrived after the second dish was served; their dinner started with the third dish.  Apparently, dishes "don't last" beyond a minute so beyond that minute, have to be thrown out.  I was appalled - I hate to see good food thrown out!  At least the late couple got to enjoy the remaining 18-21 dishes.

The atmosphere was great, the staff were amazing (5 stars for the pregnant lady!), the food was pretty freaking delicious and interesting.  All in all it was a wonderful experience.  Including the Japanese toilet.

Not recommended. I had dinner with two couples and also had the wine pairing. The meals were well thought out, the music was great and the staff was very attentive. The food itself however, was terrible. It's as if each course was meant to be great, but just fell way below the mark. There was just no flavor. The wine pairing was delivered and executed very well. For the exorbitant price, I strongly recommend you choose a different restaurant.

Every dish expertly crafted and marvelously executed.  Each one blew my mind!! 

This is our third visit to this amazing restaurant and have never been disappointed. Each time we lose count of how many  perfect and brilliant dishes  we are served.
Chef Carlo is a food genius.

Fabulous meal. Now if I'd come here before I went to Brooklyn Fare I might have been writing about one of my best dining experience ever.  But I came here afterwards. Its not Brooklyn Fare.  It is really really good - fabulous in places and very inventive (plankton for instance... who'd have thought) - ..it wasn't quite in the same league as Brooklyn Fare, though it is a very similar dining experience.  One tip which worked well here was to split a wine pairing between the pair of us: a wise choice as it meant we could remember the last few course of the meal (something which was a bit hazy from Brooklyn fare)
Ate here last year. It was insanely delicious. It ain't cheap, but we only live once (probably).

We celebrated our 5-year anniversary with dinner at Blanca. I can easily say it's one of the best meals I've ever had! The food, the service, the seating, the music--everything was amazing! So glad we lucked out with snagging ourselves a reservation. 

The tasting menu included almost 20 different plates, each delicious, some spectacular. Very inventive and well-thought out flavors, and they incorporate greens and flowers from their own garden into some of the dishes. I've been to a few tasting menus in the city (WD-50, Aska, Aldea, etc.) and this one was my favorite experience.

As some mentioned, don't be late! They start serving right on time, and if you're late, you basically miss out on the dishes they've already served. For the $$$$ you're paying for dinner, you  wouldn't want to miss any of it! 

Good luck getting a reservation, but if you do, it'll definitely be a meal you won't forget.

Very nice atmosphere and this type of 20 course dinner is definitely worth a try.  That being said  Ehh for 190 dollars per person, the taste of the food I actually tried was pretty sub par. It was all just good to okay in flavor. Interesting experience , but nothing I would return for.  Don't be late! the food comes out when it comes out and that's it!

An absolutely outstanding meal. The staff are very friendly and made everyone (myself included) feel very welcome. The restaurant is similar to Brooklyn Fare or Momofuku Ko in that the food is all cooked in front of you. A bit bigger than Brooklyn Fare and certainly bigger than Ko. If you got there early they had the king crab still alive and sitting on one of the tables- pretty cool.
I thought the food was fantastic. As with any tasting menu there were a few misses (only 1 that I frankly didn't like), most courses were good to great, and there were a few absolute home runs. Having been to both Ko and Brooklyn Fare, I thought Blanca was far better than Ko but a bit behind Brooklyn Fare. Chef Mirachi didn't use the same super expensive ingredients (truffles, caviar, fois gras) during my visit that chef Ramirez did at Brooklyn Fare, but then again the meal is much cheaper ($195 vs $255).
Overall a great experience and would highly recommend.

Wonderful experience.  This is a great place to come for a special celebration. It is very intimate and special, since there are only about 10 diners total and you are seated at a counter facing the kitchen. You can see each item being prepared pretty much from start to finish. I have been to other tastings like this, but I felt you could see the food preparation better here. The setup was comfortable, even for me at 7.5 months pregnant.
There are at least 20 courses. Many are just one bite or two, so you don't get too full but get to taste many things. I was really impressed with the foods. There were a few things on the menu I had never tasted before and there were really interesting food combos.  Each course was explained thoroughly by a really friendly staff member, as was the wine pairing. 
Excellent dining!

The place is SO cool. I adored the location. The service is great and given it is only about 10 diners total, very intimate. Only 2 sittings per night (and only open 4 nights a week). The food is good...albeit way too fishy. I'd suggest you say you are allergic to fish and skip it all together!

Everything about this restaurant is terrific, except the food. While creative and interesting, most of the 23 dishes that we ate were only good at best.  Nothing here to rave about which is a disappointment when you are spending at least $300 a person, including  wine and tip.  Go for the experience -- if you want to splurge, but don't go expecting amazing food.  The New York Times was right to give the restaurant two stars.  That is what it deserves.

Blanca is outstanding.  You will be greeted by a host at a pizza restaurant called Roberta's and escorted through the restaurant to an adjacent building.  The restaurant consists of approximately 12 seats at a counter facing the kitchen, which works best for two though at either end of the counter a party of three or four can be accommodated and converse comfortably.  There is an ideal degree of separation between the counter and the work area such that the food preparation can be observed without being "in your face".  The staff is extremely pleasant and professional and serves the more than twenty courses without excess fuss.  The menu is creative and I enjoyed all courses. 

About a month ago I had a meal at another Michelin two-star "tasting room", Atera. This also was an excellent experience though I prefer the seating counter at Blanca and the greater separation from the kitchen.  In my limited experience of one tasting menu at each, my guest and I found that the meal at Atera was more refined, and the meal at Blanca more interesting.  At each restaurant we had the wine pairing, which I preferred at Blanca.

The courses at Blanca are small.  This was OK for me, but I can envision someone with a large appetite craving pizza from Roberta's on the way out to supplement the tasting menu.

Excellent tasting dinner with an emphasis on a variety of aged meats.

***
Came here for dinner, Nov '14.

Blanca is a fine dining restaurant the seems to specialize in a variety of aged meats and seafood dishes.  The tastings tend to be more elaborate, with around 20 or so courses.  The dining environment is chef's counter only with around a dozen seats, give or take.  The ambiance is surprisingly laid back as is the personable service.  Certain diners may be interested in knowing that the restaurant holds two michelin stars as of 2014 and 2015.  Blanca is also affiliated with Roberta's next door, a more casual yet highly praised eatery that serves up a variety of pizzas, pasta, and meat dishes.

I liked Blanca a lot.  As of the end of December, I found it to be my favorite fine dining meal of the year.  Blance is from chef Carlo Mirarchi.  I first found out about him when I ate at Roberta's a few years ago, which was a great meal.  I recall he had offered tastings at Roberta's, but I never had any luck in obtaining any reservations.  Thankfully Blanca has offered that outlet with reservations now being more accessible.  

The meal I had here was spectacular.  Aside from the quicker pacing, most elements were ideal.  I especially loved the fact that so much work was put into the meats and fish prepared, often with the effect of producing a complex and bold quality of funkiness.  I found every course served was highly focused.  

There did not seem to be a lot of ingredients.  However each ingredient worked in conjunction with others very effectively.  The transition of flavors and textures were very elegant.  Meats themselves were elaborately prepared, often with lengthy aging processes.  The duck aged in its own guts and aged saddle of lamb were near perfect dishes for me.  No sous vide techniques are used when I inquired.  "They do that at Taco Bell, we don't cook our foods the same way."  Its not place for everyone, but highly rewarding for some.

Value seems quite reasonable.  For fine dining, it's a bit more expensive at around $170 per person.  There are wine pairings.  However in my case I requested some beer pairings which came out to be around $45 or so.  I found everything to be worth every penny considering how delicious everything was, the quality of ingredients, number of courses, and overall experience. 

Service was good overall.  The servers and sommalier were all very professional and laid back.  For a fine dining establishment, it truly is what I consider the best in that it manages to successfully accomplish both.  They were also knowledgeable and enthusiastic about how the dishes are prepared.  For those interested, I highly encourage interacting with the staff to find out how dishes are prepared.  It is fascinating to hear, and sadly the menu description is brief to the extent that it does all the effort put into the cooking no justice at all.

Pacing wasn't something I was entirely happy about.  I do recall there were two seating per evening.  Essentially there are three hours split between 22 courses or so, including the smaller bites in the beginning.  I found it a bit rushed to the extent where at times there was more of a pressure to finish things on time.  To be fair, the earlier small bites were quicker than the later courses.

Ambiance works well for the most part.  Its smaller space, which looks like it may have been renovated from a workshop or garage.  There's a turntable that was spinning The Misfits towards the end.  I liked how it was never formal, clinical, or stiff in any way.  The temperature was an issue.  Being that I visited in the colder months, the heater was much higher than I preferred.  There was no thermometer.  Guest at the other end of the counter found it too cold, so the heater had to be switched back and forth continually with it being either a tad warm for me, or too chilly for others.  The decor seems a bit spartan.  Acoustic levels, even with the music on was never far beyond moderate.  Overall its a good space.

Some of the dishes were quite tasty, and most were innovative.  The problems were the servers, who mostly gave off weird attitude instead of welcoming friendliness, and the quantity of the food; unless you are fat or large, there is simply too much food, and no warning sign of what and when you should skimp on - I ended up stuffing myself (hello gastritis!) as the (mostly meats by this point) kept coming and at the inflated price (especially when you add tip to the $195 base price) I didn't want to not try something.  The bread, in retrospect, should have not been served or been clearly tiny, and the meats piled on in the end (several courses in succession) should have been pruned.  Service attitude detracted immensely, and the decor is fine for a $25 dinner joint, but at this price (MORE than Le Bernardin, which has a stunning, and pricey looking decor and way better food and more innovative with pricier ingredients) it's just a money-grab on the restaurant's part (service could well be included at this price or made a flat 10%, especially as it is just ferrying dishes 2 feet, all at once).  I left with a stomach ache, and that's rich when paying so much, and going out to deep brooklyn.

Hubby  and I are in the process of checking off all the  Micheline star restaurants. Needless to say , Blanca was on the list specially since it was upgraded to a two star this year.  Personally , for us , the place didnt live up to  the expectations.

Food, in general ,  was a hit or a miss...our tasting menu boasted 20+ courses, out of which i only remember a few dishes distinctively . Wagyu beef and king crab  were phenomenal  but that pretty much was the highlight of the dinner. Dishes like ravioli with green sea plankton and  onion ice cream with shaved white truffles were rather too pretentious and unappetizing . 

We also took the wine pairing which was  at best unimpressive. Came out of the restaurant wondering if it was worth the money ...and the answer was clear, it was not. Neither the food .... and the wine pairing, most definitely NOT. 

If you really want to go there , my suggestion would be to order your own wine . The pairing includes cheap wine and does not necessarily go with the food .

How Brooklyn does fine dining. This is world class food in a restaurant that has none of the stuffiness or pretentiousness of fine dining in Manhattan. And it's absolutely amazing. You can come in with jeans and a t-shirt and experience 20+ courses of smart, creative, and immensely good food. There are vinyl records in the back that you can pick out to queue up during the meal. You can order any kind of drinks, but beer is not only acceptable but very much encouraged, as they start off your meal with a sample of their custom brew from Evil Twin.

I will defer to other reviewers for detailed descriptions of all the courses, but I will mention some things that absolutely blew me away. The pancetta, which admittedly was just pancetta, literally melted in your mouth and was fatty and salty and great. The raw wagyu beef with generous black truffle shavings was decadent, in a subtle way. The pasta dishes were really outstanding and paid a nice tribute to their famous sister restaurant, Roberta's. The plankton agnolotti bursts in your mouth and tastes like the ocean, and the nduja sausage ravioli, my favorite course of the night, was rich, spicy, and heart warming. Loved the desserts, too, which were always as savory as they were sweet, including a sour cream gelato with fried cippollini onions, poblano chile cake, and a celery root mousse at the end.

If you like food, you should go here.

This is a restaurant worth your time and attention. I get its in Brooklyn. But there are times when the food is so good you need to get in an uber and go somewhere. They are doing something worth connecting with. Each bite of the 25 courses is designed with considerable thought. Reminds me of Schwa in Chicago.

The ambience is perfect: The transparent kitchen design matched with a laid-back, casual atmosphere. There's a lot of restaurants that try to deliver series of small portion, high quality dishes that end up uneven but this nails the majority of plates. Loved it. The Duck with Mole was the best plate of the night but I've noticed the menu changes frequently. Results may vary!

Also, make sure you can handle your booze if you decide on the wine pairing. There's twelve half-glasses served over the course of the small-portion-only dinner. Not one person being served while I was there could keep up with the waitresses pouring new glasses of wine. Yes, that is a good thing.

Wow!  This place hit on all cylinders - a truly incredible food experience.  I'm always hard pressed to a meal is worth $195 per person, but this is worth it for sure.  Each taste was incredible, in over 20 dishes there were really no bummers or losers.   The Kobe beef, king crab, Lamb bucatini were memorable.  The ambiance was wonderful I'm more a fan fine dining in a relaxed setting than austere - Blanca hit a home run.  The staff and service are first rate creating an incredible evening.  Go for sure

Great staff vibe and atmosphere allowed us to relax and focus on the unusual and sometimes spectacular flavor combinations. Prince's Purple Rain ran from start to finish on a turntable behind us.

We loved the wine pairing and felt it complemented the tastings and helped transition to the next dish.

Fantastic place and experience even though we didn't enjoy the food quite as much as other high end tastings in the city.

FIVE STARS ALL THE WAY.  Felt like VIP from the moment we arrived.  Genuinely warm, friendly service the entire night.  The dishes are on par, if not better than, the 3-starred Michelin restaurants in the city.  Over 20 courses - and some of the most clever, whimsical, yet sophisticated pairings I've ever seen. 

The atmosphere is relaxed yet pristine.  Comfortable seating and a nice amount of elbow room so you're not on top of the other diners. Really enjoyed the fact that you don't have to dress like you're going on a job interview (I'm looking at you, Brooklyn Fare).  There's a fun collection of vinyl in the back, and you're encouraged to rifle through the piles to find your music for the evening.  

I should mention that they pour generously during the pairings.  Enjoy it, because at the end they give you menu cards of each course with the pairings listed in your goodie bag, so no worries if in your vermouth-stupor you can't remember what they paired the duck with. 

BLANCA is for people who know how to enjoy themselves, as well as an inventive meal.  Can't wait to go back - and soon.

While I was blown away by Blanca's exquisite dinner and super service, I'm only giving it a 4.5 stars shy of 5 stars mostly on the size of the plates. Our dinner was an impressive 19-course affair but most the dishes were "one-bite" size ( I would have prefer "two-bites" or slightly less courses); at some point I found myself filling up on the very delicious pizza bread that was serve, an indication that bigger dishes would have been appreciated.

Now the food: All the dishes were very well crafted and presented in a very delicate manner. My favorites were the king crab (which I was told had been flown to the restaurant just an hour before we arrived), the duck, carpaccio and the nduja ravioli. For dessert the pineapple sorbet, sour cream and coconut were just amazing.

Wine: I chose to try two different glasses of wine instead of doing a wine pairing and I think they were both great choices. The Arnot Roberts rose was my favorite but the Mathieu Coste Sauvignon Blanc was not very far behind.

All else: Great service and ambiance. Having "full" access to the kitchen made it much more exciting. The place is very pricey but well worth the treat. Note that in order to get in to the restaurant you will most likely have to go in through Roberta's.

It's been over a year since I visited blanca, but it left a huge impression on me. I'm incredibly excited that they were elevated to a well deserved 2 michelin stars. I'm a fan of roberta's and their pizza, but I went to blanca first. The reservations were ridiculously hard to get, and fortunately we had a friend with a diligent secretary make reservations for us. 

This restaurant only has seating for what seems like 12 people, and you walk through roberta's garden in order to enter into a shack turned luxurious modern restaurant. Watching chef carlo mirarchi cook was such a treat.  My favorite was the progression of octopus, sardines, sea perch, mackerel. I was constantly amazed at the ingredients he picked and paired together to highlight in the dishes. Every dish had that one ingredient where you were like huh? For example I was fascinated with the plankton agnolotti.. i mean really? What is that? The salt roasted potatoes, buttermilk, and chrysanthemum was also memorable. 

IF you can get reservations to this place, it's definitely worth it. If not, it's still worth the effort to try!

I've had tasting menus before at Michelin starred restaurants in The U.S. as well as Europe. I have to say that this was my favorite. 12 seats means intimacy, you're looked after very well. It also means we can all face the kitchen and see what our chef is doing. The food was fantastic, and I didn't leave feeling uncomfortable from too much overly rich food. We had 12 courses, all small and all interesting. Was it worth the bill? We think so! It's an experience worth experiencing!  Great beer list as well - some really hard to find sours if you're into that sort of thing. Bon apetit!

Walking into Blanca you forget for a fleeting moment that you're in Bushwick. The bright, airy room, state-of-the-art kitchen, and cleanliness of Bushwick's first two Michelin star restaurant is a severe contrast to the dimly lit rancor of Roberta's and the grungy neighborhood-in-transit which it inhabits. But, then, as vinyl selections begin spinning on the turntable and the unpretentious waitstaff offers up small talk, you realize, not only are you still in Bushwick, but Blanca is, despite its highfalutin accolades, distinctly Bushwick. At first, the courses felt slightly disconnected--especially compared to other, often more obvious top-rated NYC tasting menus--and I initially struggled to find logic in their progression. Some of the wine pairings were equally as curious. But, after a few dishes, I began to enjoy the eclecticism and almost anachronistic character of the courses, which, in ways I can only hope are intentional, reflected the dynamism and diversity of Bushwick itself. Every dish was perfectly executed and perfectly paced, beautifully plated on dinnerware created by local artists (of course). The ingredients were high quality, fresh, light, and summery--with produce selected that morning from local farmer's markets. A few courses were spectacular enough to write home about, including the duck, the king crab, and freshly baked pizza dough with house-made butter. Only in Bushwick, and only at a Roberta's affiliated establishment, could you serve pizza dough and butter at a $195 per person meal and be applauded for it rather than despised. Overall, Blanca lived up to expectations. Although it isn't likely the best tasting menu NYC has to offer, it's not pretending to be. Like the neighborhood it calls home, Blanca is very much an exploration, a passion-project evidenced by the choice to sacrifice seating for kitchen space, a creative journey shared with those open enough to appreciate it and, frankly, wealthy enough to afford it...there's a polemic on gentrification somewhere in there, probably between the Alaskan king crab and the pizza dough.

One of my favourite dining experiences I've ever had. Chef Carlo interacts with his diners and you get to see the cooking right in front of you all in an atmosphere with records playing, drinks flowing, and lovely hosts. They definitely make you feel welcome and comfortable while enjoying delicious food. Well worth the money!

For its price, for relatively out of the way location, and it's Michilen rating, the actual experiences  are underwhelming.  Out of 20 some courses, only 3 are at par (but not above and beyond other top chefs), the nan, the suck, the crust pork. Carlo doesn't seem to know how to cook grains and vegetables. The presentation of the courses was pretty and element , but pale compared to Blue Hill at Stone Barns, Alinea, E, Guy Savoy, Atelier Joel Rubuchon in Paris...  Blanca is not alone among big name expensive fine dining establishment, Le Pergola in Rome, Per Se here in the city, Gotham Grill, Jean George, Le Bernadine ... But that's not a good excuse. Being inventive have the risk of hit or miss, but only having 3 out out 20+ courses that are barely at par among the greats is pretty much a complete miss.  Carlo should either just stick to his meat dishes with inventive garnish, or snap out of some kind of funk or complacency and get back to the big league.
23 perfect courses, very warm & professional service, A+ dining experience. Definitely a once in a rare while price tag but worth the cost without question.

What I wrote below was before the dinner, and now this is what I'd say:

Food - 5-stars, totally deserving of all the rave. Creative, tasty, sensory orgasm is what I would call it.  I really wish we could talk to the chef more about his inspirations.  Such a humble and beautiful artist.

Service - 1-star, because I have never seen more snobbish rubbish from a front end staff that had no idea what service really means.  I should not get this type of dismissive attitude anywhere, and especially not when you might be expecting at hefty tip.  

To the front end staff at Blanca -- if it makes you uncomfortable to be nice, don't work in the service industry... really.  Do us and your restaurant a favour.

**
I was very excited for my reservations at Blanca this week, but our correspondence with "Reservations" today have really been a huge disappointment. I like to start all my restaurant experiences at a high base (glass half full), but given today's unnecessary and snobbish interaction, I'm going to have to start at a 2 and see if they remedy this, or really win me over on the food so much that I can look pass the extremely self-righteous and nonsensical treatment.  So far, I've experience much better at any other michelin-starred (or even un-starred) restaurants.  To be continued...

We shall see how it goes after the dinner. After much fan fare today, I have yet to receive more information about the wine pairing offered, and we were told that despite having two confirmed bookings, we have to ask one friend to drop out because our two parties combined would be 5 people, and that's above the 4 people rule. Reminds me of when airlines overbook... D'oh!

We heard many good things about this restaurant before we went, and it definitely lived up to the expectations. I'd like to lead off with a few cautionary tips for people who are planning to go there, because I know no one finishes reading long reviews.

(1) Allow for additional traveling time. This place is officially difficult to find, and you aren't even sure whether you've got to the right place when you indeed have. Google maps is accurate (thank God!), but we were surprised that the check-in point was actually in that overly-crowded pizza/bar place. Anyway, if you are planning to go on the weekend, definitely leave early because subway trips into Brooklyn on the weekend can take significantly longer than what Google maps tell you, and I speak as a proud resident of Brooklyn.

(2) Try the wine-pairing (which is really an alcohol-pairing, as it doesn't restrict the selection to wines). It's good and relatively inexpensive. 

(3) Bring a shawl, ladies, if you go on a hot summer day. I regretted not bringing one, and as dinner progressed I began to have a stomachache. The servers did turn down the air-conditioning for us, but that didn't do the trick for me. My stomach was upset for quite some time, and I was sure it was the temperature.

(4) As there are many seafood items on the menu, seafood-haters should probably think twice. I'm not saying that the pork or the duck wasn't impressive, but the stars of the night were definitely the seafood courses. They can accommodate food allergies pretty well, but their seafood dishes were so good that it's a shame to remove them. 

What we truly loved about this place was its originality. Food at this place (and the wine-pairing) was comparable to a Michelin 2-star or even a 3-star restaurant (as was the price, I might add), so I'll save my breath and stop complimenting it further. The atmosphere is nice, too, as all diners (regardless of when you arrive) start having the same dish at (roughly) the same time at the same long table, which prompts people into chatting occasionally with total strangers sitting next to them about the food. I liked that, but I'm not sure if that would be a little too much for people who prefer to have quiet dinners by themselves on their own table. I saw that a fellow reviewer hated the service there, but I liked the servers so I thought I should mention it here as well. The servers were warm and helpful - not snobbish at all.

I was very disappointed by Blanca. I had read so many wonderful reviews about them, yet I was not pleased by the menu. The only thing I found exciting was the secret path I had to travel before being seated. 

Here is my complaint: the food was not good. Of the 19 courses only about 7 were actually good and only 3 of those were exceptional (meaning I couldn't make a better tasting version at home). 

And let me add that I have been to Eleven Madison Park, that food was completely exquisite from start to finish. They had a menu that I couldn't replicate on my best day in the kitchen.

Sorry Blanca, presentation was fantastic, and even the plating was good for the most part but the food was barely better than high school lunch.  At more than $200 a person your food should be much much better than it was.

Really awkward check in. You are made to wait in the Tiki bar of Roberta's.
Food was pretty good but not amazing and not worth the $$$.

Blanca is a restaurant hidden behind Roberta's pizzeria in the heart of Bushwick. The feeling of a speakeasy adds to their 2 star Michelin experience. 

The setting is very intimate with only a 12 person seating at the bar. They only take reservations Wednesday - Saturday with 6:00 and 9:30 seating options available...cause they're can and they're that cool.

The food is very new American experimental; which makes it stand out - paprika pepper on baby corn, eggplant with ceviche, even oven baked break from Robertas.. of the 19 course dinner, I felt like it was hit or miss and that is why I have to retract a star.

They have a record player with albums in which patrons are more than free to play to their liking. 

Blanca does a fine job representing the essence of the neighborhood with the upscale fine dining twist.

I have mixed feelings about this place. Food was indeed impeccable with no misses at all - I especially enjoyed the duck with beet sauce (have to try this out) and the king crab leg (so tender). Chef and waiter were extremely helpful and the whole tasting process was indeed remarkable.

On the other hand, I felt a bit disappointed as we arrived about ten minutes late so unfortunately missed the first two courses. We were not even being informed about that until I checked the number of courses! No wonder my friend was saying that there was simply not enough food! This was actually the first time we have encountered this issue. I know we also had part of the responsibility however the experience was not longer flawless. 

To be fair, I gave them five star for taste of food, deducting one for still being hungry afterwards and another one for an incomplete version of tasting.

I read some of these reviews after dining there on 10/30 so here's my thoughts/responses. Ambiance was fun, and yes the maze into the room added to the charm. I didn't feel a pretentious bone from any of the service staff - so friendly and accommodating. I did wish the kitchen would interact with us though since its such a personal experience. I left hungry and literally had to go get a second meal which just shouldn't happen (the couple next to us did the same). My wagyu was not quite right and I left 1/3 - too bad. Otherwise I really enjoyed the meal so please don't read my critiques as negative, in the context of the whole night they are minor. Someone below also complained about being late and missing courses - we all received emails saying you will miss courses if you are late out of respect for the other diners, so that really wasn't a fair review.

Just as an orchid isn't any ordinary flower, Blanca is far from just a restaurant. Blanca is an experience. The dishes were carefully executed and beautifully presented. None of this would matter though if it wasn't for the exceptional ingredients- i.e. house-cured prosciutto was melt-in-your-mouth good. One or two bites for each dish was just enough to satisfy every time (except the stracciatella, they can scratch that off the menu immediately. This was surprising given the amazing stracciatella starter at Roberta's). Each dish is so thoughtful and hits on all umami notes that it captivates you in that moment and makes you forget all about the previous course. If it wasn't already official that I am a carnivore, the Game Pie put the stamp on it. It was decadent and comforting like a homemade dinner you can only get from your grandmother's kitchen. The wine pairing was interesting and completed the experience. Though it was exceptionally expensive, it was an experience we will never forget. You can't put a price tag on that.

ok quite quite quiiiiiite lovely
so lovely
yes - it's a special occassion kind of place
so splurge for it and go w an empty belly
eventhough the dishes r petit
they fill you up
quiet, fun sophisticated & super tasty
i had some legit dishes and i do feel for the ones who didnt
i cant recommend dishes because it changes 
but i do recommend blanca quite so

There is nothing wrong w Blanca... Until you get your check and you realize that there is a price to living well in NYC. 

1. Get the drink pairing.  We had wines, cider, beer, sake, etc. and each noticeably made the dish taste better. It was incredible and tasty 

2. Don't sit at the ends. You'll freeze in the winter 

3. Everything is made w care. The guy took a good 15 min to make our tea at the end of dinner

4. Your favorite course will be the pizza bread. And you'll have wished you asked for more Bc likelihood of another $600 meal here in the next month(s) will be rare. It will also be the shaved foie gras. Or the wagyu or the pasta. But quite clearly could be the game pie. 

5. I ate plankton dumplings and it was good.

Creative, easy vibe and most dishes are very delicious. Some plates were on a bit heavy side though. Worth a visit for sure and a slice of the incredible pizza at the front. Also, do the wine pairing with the meal- incredibly compliments the experience and food.

Amazing experience.  The service was impeccable and not pretentious.  All of the food was delicious and the wine pairing was AMAZING - I would even say the wine pairing menu was better than the actual food menu!  Favorite course was the Roberta's pizza dough and homemade butter.  Only reason I don't give this place 5 stars is I could've used an course or two more to leave fully stuffed!  The bite-sized portions left me wanting more!

I am leaving a very expensive meal and wine pairing at Blanca hungry and sober.  The food was very very good, and if that is all you care about you will probably love it.  I however found the setting cold, the very visible turntable playing sabbath as background music just too much (I mean seriously?  How cool are you?) and the portions laughably tiny.  I believe they cooked one steak for 20 people.  Expense account only.

I've been to Roberta's in the past, but for my birthday, my wife decided to take me to Blanca next door. We weren't quite sure how to get in at first, so we went in the entrance for Roberta's, where someone was waiting to take us through the dining area, outside, and then to the sparsely decorated room where there are about a dozen seats facing a similarly sparse kitchen (e.g. you don't have loads of copper pots hanging as you do at Chef's Table). The hostesses were great, getting out dishes in front of us like clockwork, with the chef taking a break to serve us one dish (the fresh bread). Despite sitting at a bar with everyone, it is a very relaxing experience, although the folks to our right were a bit of a nuisance in speaking loudly and breaking up the atmosphere a bit. That said, when you have Metallica and punk rock blaring from the record player (the hostesses and even some of the cooks would come out and switch up the music from time to time), it already has a more casual, definitively 'Brooklyn' feel to it than most restaurants of this caliber.

As for dinner itself - what a treat. I count 19 courses (which are really more like bites for the most part) on the menu that was provided, with a general inspiration from Italian cuisine but a meal that was uniquely American. The beginning was very interesting, as we wavered back and forth between mellow dishes with subtle flavors and dishes with bright, distinctive flavors and notes. The glass shrimp with kohlrabi and poppy seeds had a very smooth texture and clean taste to it, with a slight sweetness from the shrimp. That was followed, though, by a slice of very fatty pancetta, along with a nicely-aged and textured slice of prosciutto. The squid was also a very clean flavor, with almond broth giving it a nutty undertone that contrasted nicely to small slices of citrus. The Romanesco soup was excellent and drizzled with a little spice, giving it a nice, bold flavor without being overly hot. The apple with foie gras shavings, while very interesting to watch being prepared (I thought it was a good helping of cheese being added to the dish from further away), was actually my least favorite dish of the night - a little too mellow, with the meal just making it a very plain dish. The foie gras added some creaminess but not too much else in terms of flavoring. The lightly crisped purple potato was great, though - another broth infused with nuts (this time macadamia) made it a nice, homey dish with a flavor profile that stood out a bit more from a regular potato.

From here, we took a diversion towards the more overtly Italian parts of the meal, starting with the lamb carbonara - one of my favorite courses of the night. Along with the caramelle and ravioli, you can tell the pasta here is made with great care and cooked to perfection from a texture standpoint - each bite of pasta was done probably slightly more than al dente, with a very nice firmness to it. The lamb tasted excellent in the carbonara, with a heavy dosing of salt and freshly ground pepper to give it a bit of heat. The caramelle, served in a tea broth, was a bit more on the mellow side but still had great texture. The ravioli, filled with a smooth andouille sausage spread, went back to the more flavorful side again. The last dish in this section of the meal, before the 'main courses', was the stracciatella - very fresh and delicious, especially when paired with a small piece of beef lard, infusing it with a different strain of fatty goodness.

The mains were all phenomenally done, with the king crab first up. You have to scrape out all the meat yourself, but when dipping it in a thick sauce made from a puree of salted fish roe, it is an intensely delicious seafood course. Next up - surprise! - is a large hunk of pizza dough bread! It's by far the largest course of the dinner, and serving it with the rest of the mains is an interesting choice - but it is so amazingly delicious, especially with the butter on it, that I scarfed it down in minutes. We then went back to the wagyu-style beef, which had great flavor and a crispy piece of fat that adds more succulence to each bite. Then it was time for a palate cleanser - a grapefruit puff that was quite smooth and paired with wheatgrass juice - before enjoying a game pie, served with slice of duck breast. It was the least distinct part of the mains but still had great, hearty flavors without being overly heavy (although the horseradish shavings were a bit of an odd note). Desserts finished up the meal, with it having a more savory take than one would anticipate. The sourdough gelato with yuzu was a very nice, mellow first bite. Next up was sunchoke(!) - also quite delicious, along with being a bit on the heavier side. Cashew and coconut gelato was next, served over candied walnuts - a nutty, tasty finish.

Definitely a great meal, and one that I would recommend others to come enjoy - a delicious fine dining experience with a much more casual feel to it!

A must go in New York, I think. Blanca is simply phenomenal. Environment is relatively casual (definitely not a blazer required restaurant, nor a "formal" restaurant).

You'll get courses in the high-teens and the food is all delicious with every bite (and each course is a bite or two at the most).They also spend the entire dinner preparing this duck in front of you that they will serve at the apex of the meal--and the duck is honestly incredible. We actually thought the pasta dishes they did were ok, but everything else they served was creative and delicious (AND THE ROBERTA'S PIZZA DOUGH FRESH OUT OF THE OVEN; my gosh it's so good).

You should order the drinks pairings--pairings are very eclectic (they served a wine out of Evil Twin brewery which I thought was pretty interesting)

Service is very good. You check in at the restaurant portion of Roberta's (not the take out section). I made a reservation ~3 weeks in advance which is roughly when they open the calendar up for reservations. 

And you get to play records that everyone listens to on their vinyl. I wish they added a Kendrick record but they have a good collection of '90s hip hop, David Bowie, some classic albums, etc.

We received a goodie bag with a delicious, delicious smore at the end and overall thought this was one of the best fine dining places we went.

Oh my goodness absolutely the best. 

My boyfriend booked this place on Valentine's weekend and we had the greatest time. It's a two star Michelin restaurant tucked behind Roberta's Pizza in Bushwick (owned by the same owner) so you feel like you are discovering a new world when you enter the restaurant. 

You're seated at the bar facing an open kitchen. The server walks around to each person with their food or wine course and explanations. I love sitting at bars and counters by default as it contributes to a more casual atmosphere and I love open kitchens so this arrangement was perfect for me. The one thing I will say is because the servers went systematically from person to person and we were all seated relatively close to one another, you almost felt like you were listening to a record over and over again. The servers did try to change up their explanations for variety's sake to mitigate this though. Another plus is you have the opportunity to put on what the music you want to listen to by choosing from their collection of records. They have a pretty large and decent collection. 

The meal itself is a 19 course meal. My favorites were the pizza dough (the popular option I think) and the duck which they start preparing during the first course but was one of the last courses we had. 

Lastly, I would definitely recommend getting the drink pairings. Most of the drinks they served us were from breweries or wineries that they had preexisting relationships with and were very creative.
We went there for birthday celebration, very good food with the right portion. Have to say it's the most impressive one I tried among all those three stars restaurants in NYC.
the food is really good, BUT it is a bit pricey for me (I ended up paying $750 for two people). Now I have to eat instant ramen for the whole month...

Obviously, this is an experience. Just like the chef table's of..Chef's Table, Atera, etc.  I guess the food's more inventive because this is Brooklyn, and this is Roberta's, but each dish is really excellent and top notch. They change the menu frequently, and you don't know what you're getting (they just ask if you have allergies) but that's part of the show. Though, I should say it's not much of a "show" because the kitchen is surprisingly quiet.. the chef are hard at work. The minimalist white decor though, is gorgeous.  And the servers are very fun, do a good job of explaining your meal/wine...but overall..are more zen and quiet. The whole atmosphere is really..cerebral.  The tableware/plates are very modern and cool. My fiance took me for my birthday,  and they sat us on the end.  Be SURE you are not late for your seating.  We arrived like legit a minute before, and everyone was already there, and they were about to start.  Also, what can be a hold up is that Blanca is hidden inside Roberta's, so be sure you bypass the people waiting in line for pizza and walk up right to the host so you're not held up. 

We had 19 courses.  We did the wine pairing, which was a steal because of the amazing wines you try with each meal.  The meal was overall.. a bit imbalanced, being it was very veggie heavy, and white wine heavy.  They didn't showcase the meat as much nor the reds. But regardless, everything was excellent - these folks are master of flavor.   We had: 

- A micro brewed beer made in house, refreshing in a cold cold glass, they call it Evil Twin, kind of had a saison taste

- glass shrimp with kohlrabi and poppy seed- crunchy fun
- pancetta- cured in house, nice and fatty
- garbanzo bean - fried beans with a garbanzo green puree, deliciously smokey and yummy
-upstate apples with macademia nuts, very smoky, nutty, flavorful. This dish was great when eaten all together
-sweet potato - fried, with greens and buttermilk, VERY tasty
-peas with ramps, of course it's spring. This was a bit similar to the above, for me
- Carbonara with lamb sausage or bacon- WOW to have a bite of this is a really a tease. The perfect al dente pasta and cheesy carbonara meets salty meat, my favorite of the night, YUM YUM YUM
-Agnlotti - delicate pasta bites that were equal parts oolong tea (legit) and cheese, delicious 
-Nduja Ravioli- just one but spiced with cajun seasoning and andouille sausage, very spicy and flavors spot on
-Straacciatella - everyone's favorite cheese, with beef lardo bites- great texture
-King Crab with lemon butter- VERY yummy. 
- Fresh bread aka Roberta's pizza dough, with house butter and more lemon butter from the crab. Dough is amazeeeee (naan like, chewy, charred, yummy) and the butter was perfectly salted. Might have been my second fave.
-Beef - rare waygu with greens, delish 
- House brewed kombucha, very big on tea flavor 
-Yummy pork with grapefruit and turnip, flavorful, well done, fatty.. we got a second piece 

Dessert:
-Sourdough gelato- kind of that a dry, bready flavor- definitely got sourdough 
-Sunchoke cake - a crispy cake with spices like cardamom; didn't taste the sunchoke much but it was crispy and well done
-Cashew - spot on nutty ice cream, with good coconut flavor 
-Chocolate brittle with peanut butter, yum. 

The wine pairing (and by the way, you can potentially get more than one glass- depends on what you drink; your glass is always full)

- Huges Godme Champagne, yum
-Venica & Vernice Sauv Blanc, my favorite grape
-Colosia - Amontiallado- a type of sherry, which was dry at first but finished sweet
-Clos de Trias- a Rose that I actually liked; not too dry
-Montegioco- a wheaty beer, yum
-Francois Chidaine - a crisp, perfect white
-Huia - Pinot Noir, didn't love it but I don't know anything about pinot noir 
-Cieck- a full bodied Piedmont
-Hermann Wiemer Riseling- sweet... don't love Riesling

Also, I celebrated my birthday here and they kindly gave me a nice birthday card and put a candle in our last course (the brittle).  We also got a Smore's sandwich as a to-go present.

5 Stars for the masterful food, flavors, complexity of each dish, yes.  5 Stars for beautiful decor and zen restaurant, and the friendly service.  5 stars for the WINE, and for them not judging me because I got drunkizzle. 

Now here's the thing. Minus one star because for a $300 per head dinner, we left hungry.  Yes there were 20 courses but each was legit.. a bit. A tease. A taste, i guess it is a tasty dinner but for $300 a head my philosophy is that you should not leave hungry.  Being that I have never been to Roberta's proper, I decided to take out a Famous Original pizza which was a delicious ,eat-at-home present.

Finally, a Michelin restaurant that lives up to the hype! We arrived two courses tardy but the sweet staff made sure to serve them to us. I was so confused as we walked through Roberta's at first, but it was pure joy as we entered the airy space at Blanca. What's true has all been said--the food is minimally portioned but inventive and delicious. I especially loved our plankton dish--I didn't even know you could eat plankton! It was such a joy to watch our food being prepared and seeing Chef Mirarchi work his magic. 

Loved the format of the chef's table and we friended the lovely couple beside us. The whole experience was leisurely, fascinating, and educational. We were still a bit hungry at the end of the dinner so along with our new friends next to us, each bought a pie from Roberta's. The server offered to put in the order at course 16 or 17 so that the pie would come out right on time as we ended the meal. 

The little jars of peanut butter to take home at the end of the meal were a delightful surprise. Couldn't think of a better way to end the experience than to take a little piece of Robertas home. Thanks Blanca for the wonderful memories!

I really enjoyed my 2.5-hour tasting course at Blanca. Having read other reviews on Yelp, I thought I might need to order a pizza at the end. Since you walk through Roberta's to get to Blanca, my bf and I eyed people's delicious-looking pizza on our way in. We checked in at where we were on the "pizza meter" throughout the night. At first we were at 100% pizza given that we were super hungry, but after the fresh dough course, he was down to 30% and we were full by the end of the dinner. They gave us ridiculously delicious smores as a treat to take home, too.

Each course is only a few bites, but they're packed with flavors and beautifully presented. To me, a great tasting menu like this requires two things: 1) inventive use of ingredients that 2) work well together aka taste is on point. Blanca achieved both of these with flying (minimalist) colors. Particular standouts to me were the garbanzo bean soup, apple with macadamia shavings that melted in the mouth, chewy and rich carbonara, nduja sausage ravioli, sunchoke cake with cardamom and chocolate for dessert, and the fresh dough. If you're asking yourself, how good can pizza dough taste? Try some when it's steaming hot. It really tastes that good. 

I also much prefer this laid-back more casual environment without the pretension of some three-star Michelin restaurants like Per Se and Eleven Madison Park. It's not a place to be seen, but rather a place to focus on the food and the experience of watching people absorbed in their craft.

The best meal that I've had so far this trip to NYC. I've been wanting to go since my cousin mentioned it about 4 years ago. It was hard to get a reservation, but the wait is totally worth it. Many little bites that you think won't fill you up, but you end up full and happy you came. The food is creative and the staff is super attentive. Very comfortable environment, the staff makes you very much at home. Leslie loves her job and you can definitely see it in the way she answers questions, explains each dish and the warmth that exudes. Thanks to the staff for making my birthday trip to NYC so special. Each dish was a pleasant surprise on the palette. 

My favorites:
King crab with bottarga butter
Agnolotti with Lapsang Souchong tea
Nduja ravioli
Apple macadamia

Quite an amazing meal.  Loved the way the restaurant felt and how it was a maze to get to it through Roberta's.  Definitely made it feel more special.  Best dish- Agnolotti infused with lapsang souchong.  The bottarga served with the King Crab is also quite unfairly good.  Great eclectic mix of a ton of cuisines blended together...Italian, French, Japanese, Spanish, Korean, Chinese, American.  Loved the sourdough gelato with yuzu combo as well.  Very memorable experience.

My husband and I had a terrific dinner at Blanca's in May when we were hanging out in Brooklyn for the weekend. We took a stroll around the neighborhood to check out the street art before dinner. It's a good idea to arrive early since if you're late they'll start service without you and you could miss a course or two. They are very clear about this when you make the reservation.  It's an interesting area to explore so it's worth coming ahead of time.

You enter through Roberta's and there's a long line for that,but just bypass it and see a host directly.  We had to hang out in Roberta's for a few minutes and had a good look at the pizza and other dishes in Roberta's and they looked terrific.  You're lead through the back garden to Blanca's where you're seated on comfortable padded stools with backs at the counter overlooking the kitchen.  We loved the eclectic soundtrack!  Everyone was incredibly nice, from the host to the team of chefs who served us.  We just loved the overall vibe of the place.  Unfortunately there was a lone Japanese guy on one side of us who didn't seem keen to engage and a couple on the other side who kept to themselves, so we didn't socialize except with the chefs. At the other end of the counter all of the couples were chatting with each other so it can be a convivial experience if you're in the right spot. 

It's been too long to recall all of the food details, however we enjoyed every creative dish and the beverage pairings were very good as well. I hate beer but had a few sips of the one they offered and while it was unusually good for beer, it was still beer, so not my favorite pairing.  We're accustomed to tasting menus and this style of dining at places like Momofuku Ko so we weren't surprised. We have to say that Blanca's was among our favorites.

If it's possible to give zero star, Blanca would get zero star for service.  Blanca NEVER picks up the phone.  You can only make a reservation online.  We made ours 30 days in advance for a special birthday celebration.  It was confirmed two weeks in advance when we emailed Blanca to let them know that one person in the party doesn't eat pork.  After arranging for a babysitter for our special night, we show up to be told that our reservation was cancelled 5 weeks earlier!?!?   How is that possible when we got a confirmation 2 weeks earlier from the restaurant???  After telling us what appears to be a blatant lie, the hostess leaves us waiting at the bar "to figure out what happened."  Half an hour later, she shows up to offer us a table at Roberta's.  Not on them.  They were offering us the special privilege of taking one of Roberta's empty tables at 5:30pm so that they can make money off of us after ruining our night.  Thanks, but no thanks.  They also offered us the chance to come back to Blanca another night.  Blanca needs to realize that when you want to charge  $200+/ per meal per person, a restaurant needs to provide excellent service as well as excellent food.  A $200+ meal is a special occassion for most people.  Blanca managed to totally ruin it for us.

Unfortunately, Blanca let us down and made my wife's big birthday memorable for the wrong reason. I can't comment on the food, which we never got to taste. She made the hard-to-get reservation a month in advance. Our party of four (including two special guests) arrived from all around the city for what we hoped would be a transcendent meal. In anticipation, we'd all skipped lunch. We arrived (early) and were told, inexplicably, that our reservation (though it had been confirmed, twice) couldn't be honored. No call, no email, just a hard to believe excuse about Blanca phasing in a new computer system or some such. Maybe it's something they got with their new Tisch family private equity cash? To be clear, Blanca fully acknowledged its mistake, but offered only cold consolation: Nothing could be done to seat us that evening, sorry. Well Blanca, Blanquita, this seems like goodbye. Time to hail an Uber and find a last minute salvage option for a now disappointed birthday girl. I'm not sure we'll be meeting again.

Echoing other comments - the food was very innovative and the place tops the list of tasting menus to try. The carbonara, sweet potato, Strawberry wrap and wagyu beef top the list. However, my favourite was the pizza dough!!!!! 

Side note; they have a record player and the space is great.

Star docked only because reviews said you would be comfortably full but we were not - this is not always a fair dock as ppls stomach's are diff sizes!
Mmmm... NO. Went here for my birthday a few years ago. Not for me. Really strange and pretentious food. Priced high and served diner style which left us all scratching our heads.

The food at Blanca was wonderful, particularly the dry-aged beef, which was one of the best pieces of beef I have ever eaten. Almost everything looked great and tasted as good as it looked. I have two major complaints, however:

1. The portions were tiny, and we left hungry. There's a reason I referred to the beef we ate as a "piece" of beef. It was a one-square inch chunk, and that's about as large as any dish gets. To be sure, we didn't eat much earlier in the day, but still, it's surprising that, after 20 courses (or, really, 20 bites of food) here, we went around the corner to Moku Moku (the new sister restaurant to the always amazing Momo Sushi Shack), and had a big salad and two full dishes.

2. My biggest complaint is the service. Usually when you're paying this much for a restaurant, the service is phenomenal and the servers make you feel fully attended to. While the sommelier was nice, the two main waitresses were cold, formal and rude. Each time they dropped off a plate, they rushed through a mumbled rendition of the ingredients as though they were in a real rush to move on, so that we were often turning to each other right afterwards with a "did you catch that?" "no." It was just a recited laundry list, not any expression of care or pride. As at many high-end restaurants, there were often uncommon ingredients they mentioned that we weren't familiar with, and when we'd ask what that was, they'd almost look annoyed at having to explain. More egregiously, each time they brought a plate out or took something away, we said, "Thank you." We did not get a single, simple, "You're welcome." Not even a glance of acknowledgement or a smile. They just left and moved on. We kept saying thank-you, ever-more loudly and clearly, and still not once did we get a response. The fact that both servers acted like this almost makes it seem like a thought-out policy ("don't pause too long at any diner; 'you're welcomes' slow things down). Service like this can transform what should be a great dining experience into a sense that the restaurant is just going through the motions, anxious to get you fed and out the door. I don't need the servers to fawn over me, but a bit of common courtesy and ordinary social graces would be nice. And, indeed, we encountered a huge contrast when we went around the corner to Moku Moku. The irrepressible Phillip Gilmour described each ingredient in his food with care and pride, answered all our questions with pleasure, gave us a large complimentary pork chop (that was amazing, by the way) after hearing about our frustrating experience at Blanca and made us feel at home. Guess which restaurant we'll be coming back to and telling our friends about.

Super great experience at Blanca NYC. This is a tasting menu restaurant in Bushwick. No Menu - you eat what they cook up that day. Super expensive with food, drinks and impeccable service to match. Goes to show how much this city (NYC) has to offer and keep surprising me every time.   If you think this spot is pretentious, you'll have a great and friendly surprise.

Great setting. 
It's awesome to watch chefs to their work. 
Menu while creative is a but over-the-top in its desire to be creative, while
leaving you unsatisfied in some of the essential. 
I would totally add another star had it been 40% cheaper. The cost is also over the top.
My guess I'd have enjoyed Roberta's a lot more for the fraction of the price.

So disappointed! I'll start by saying the vibe is great. As well as the space. Clean, simple, comfortable, exclusive. Staff was super friendly and on point. 
 
Now the food.... 18 course tasting menu. Privy to coming we new this was going to be an experience. Bite sized wonders of joy. Michelin stars! Ughhhhh, out of the 18 bites, there were probably about 3 that were intensely creative and bursting with flavor. One being the pizza dough they make at Roberto's pizzeria. Once you got through the burnt ashes, it was warm and yummy! Most of the courses were of little substance and underwhelming flavor. ( piece of cantaloupe and a piece of watermelon with a silver of macadamia nut)? Snore! Perhaps a palate cleanser but a course?? We did the wine pairing as well. They barely topped the stems. Perhaps 2 sips per course was poured. Very chincy for $95pp. If it totaled 2 full glasses by the end of the meal I would be surprised. I was at least hoping to be buzzed by the time the $700 bill came. We almost felt the staff went in the back after the seating and were like "suckers". Nothing left you craving another bite at all. No comparison to EMP or Per se.

Last one on the Michelin 2 star list. Check

Located inside Roberta's (a restaurant within a restaurant).

The 18-course tasting menu - very unique/creative; basically 1-or 2-bites per course (so recommend a late lunch before coming).
The pacing here is a little on the quicker side (you will done with all the courses around 2 hrs).

Very nice/relaxing atmosphere w/ classic music (Bowie, Talking Heads, etc.) playing in the background.

The chef de cuisine was out today, so the head chef from Roberta's filled in and did a marvelous job preparing all the courses with the rest of the kitchen staff. 

Enjoyed most of the courses. My favs were the pancetta, melon, sweet potato, pea/foie gras, agnolotti, nduja ravioli, king crab, fresh bread, beef okra, and the pork. Nice use of edible flowers for presentation.

3 desserts (Mostly different types of sorbets; Enjoyed the cashew/coconut sorbet the most.)

Excellent service.

Highly recommended.

: 9 calendars

-----------------------------------------------------------
Go with the wine pairing - $85 - (A good deal; Got to try some very unique wines, including smoked beer from Tennesse, a great 4-year old Japanese sake, etc.)

Tasting menu is $195, which doesn't include tax/gratuity, so expect to spend total around $350 pp, if you get the wine pairing, which I recommend (compliments the food very well).

I hate to say this, but I did not enjoy a single thing about this restaurant.

The food was not pleasant at all. I consider myself as a very open-minded and creative customer, but the concept and the whimsical sense the chef trying to blend into the dishes were not enjoyable at all for me. To be honest, I did not enjoy any one of the 19 courses... not even the lamb carbonara, which I thought was something that can't go wrong. The desserts were unpalatable either - I can see they are trying to blend flavors and be inventive but the combination really did not come out so great.

The service and attitude is another thing - unpleasant... no one worked there looked happy or friendly. My friends and I did not enjoy the dinner - it was not worth the price or the trip to Brooklyn.

There were so many courses that I lost track of how many their were. I loved the vibe that was complete with a record player, playing all their music. I loved watching the kitchen prepare/plate the food. I opted not to get the alcohol pairing, however I wish I did because of the amount of courses and I was jealous of the people sitting beside me who had gotten it. However I did order drinks by the glass and they eagerly helped me to pick the best wine/sake for me, even picked some that were not on their wine by the glass list. When I come back to nyc, it will definitely be on my list to try again.

Very fantastic cuisine. Exceptional creativity and quality of the ingredients. I had some of the best crudo and meat dishes here at Blanca. So what is the negative???

The issue I had is despite the plentiful courses, each one is literally 1 bite and one arguably won't be full by the end of the meal. With the extremely high price tag one would expect to be quite full after. Believe me when I decided to walk over to robertas takeout after my 230 dollar a person dinner for a slice. I also wasn't particularly impressed by an attempt to be filled by the cooks with pizza dough as a course that of course was as filling as the previous 5 courses of delicacies and interesting dishes. I believe that the quality of the food is 4.5 to 5 stars here, but at this price range - I need to feel full when I'm done! The fact that you have to walk past yummy smelling robertas pizzas to get to the back room, at 20 dollars a pop certainly doesn't help the situation. I would urge the Blanca staff to make each course just a tad bit bigger. By the way, I'm a slender male at 150 pounds so just imagine if I had a big appetite!

We tried Blanca's tasting menu on 1/26/17.  The location is a little bit tricky and requires you to walk through a bar, saturated with the smell of sweat and booze.  Blanca is hidden behind Roberta's in a contemporary dining room.  Its kitchen is open-viewing, giving diners a chance to see the preparation of each and every meal and the venue has very limited seating (perhaps 8 or 10 people?).  

The menu was an eighteen-course tasting that left me pretty satisfied by the end of the experience.  However, there seemed to be a slightly extended delay between the courses that left a little more than ample time for conversation.  Each course, though, was considerably appetizing and the cleanse courses help ensure a full appreciation of the flavors.  My favorite courses were the mackerel, which had distinct nodes of lemon as well as the wagyu beef, which was broiled very nicely.  Their bread was a nonconventional kind of pizza dough, but was warm and an appropriate precursor to the subsequent dishes.  Presentation was impeccable, each dish as visually alluring as its taste. They were quite chancy in deciding to use spices and I thought it didn't accompany certain courses well, especially with the clam.  The dessert, cashew coconut, was also a little heavy for liking, especially as a final course.

Overall though, a very pleasant experience with an equally pleasant staff.

I loved Blanca. You are a bit thrown off at first. You get an email with fairly rigid instructions about being on time or they'll start without you and that they don't accommodate severe allergies or dietary restrictions. Then you show up at Roberta's, a loud hipstery pizza place in Bushwick. Then you remember you're in Bushwick. And about to shell it at least $2-300 for a dinner. 

Quickly that apprehension went away once you're brought into Blanca and given something to eat. The space in large and white, a bit industrial. A lot of beastie boys, Bowie, and other hipsters music playing. 

But wow, the food. My first bite was a revelation and made me happy. It continued from there. The food is innovative, flavorful and fun. You sit at a bar facing the open kitchen. We opted to skip the pairing and got some great sake. 

The food is truly excellent. A few towards the end were very good but not great. But out of the many many courses, those were the exceptions. The staff is very friendly. 

The pizza bread served as part of a course is outstanding. Hard not to buy a pizza on your way out. We were full, but not overly so. 

Highlights were: Highlights were the einkorn with lardo, watermelon radish with coriander, celeryroot, maitake with uni and Asia pear, sweet potato with a kick, maine shrimp with the head, pasta with clams, nduja ravoili (a spicy favorite), and insane pizza dough. The rice pudding was my favorite dessert.

The expectations of a two starred restaurant is high, and Blanca just fell short of it. They are not in the same league as Atera; who are two starred as well with the open kitchen bar seating concept. 

I don't believe either the service or the food were up to par. Both were quite bland. I would not consider the service pretentious or rude as other reviews stated, but there was just no warmth or friendliness from any of the wait staff. They all seemed quite disinterested and extremely brief with their descriptions. 

This may be one of the first experiences I've had at a Michelin starred restaurant (and I've had very many) that I was not "wow'd" by a single dish. The only honorable mentions were the pasta with squab ragu and the delicious pizza dough from roberta's. Every other dish was either bland, uninventive, or just unappetizing. It also seems as if they're controlling their food cost trying to use less expensive ingredients for most of the dishes. One of the courses with raw clams contained shells and grit in both mine and my partner's. This was handled well as it was mentioned to the chef and he graciously removed one of our wine pairing fees (which was a hit or miss, more often being misses). 

In short, I was disappointed. I was on the fence between two or three stars, but because of the accolades and the expectations that it brings, I settled with two.
