I can't say that i was able to enjoy blanca; i booked on the wrong date by mistake and they went and charged me 430 dollars anyway. They don't even call to confirm the date and time as all restaurants of this supposed calibre do. How tacky. Needless to say i won't be going there (ever)

Incredible food, presentation and atmosphere. Not stuffy like a lot of the Michelin restaurants. 
You can fee the passion of the staff working there. Can't wait to go back.

This is meal number two of an insane week of dining. 

Recommended to Blanca as was told it's the hippy cool Italian influence version of atera which was amazing. 

Yup everything u expected!  Start in the pizza bar. With weird hipster waitress telling us we can't stand there. I'm lady, we were told to. 
"Noooo one would tell u that"
- wrong - Blanca person did. 
Yah weird start. :)

Anyhow super chill and cool vibe. Vinyl player with diner choice. Atera is the suit and tie version. This is untucked shirt and cool blue shoes version. 

Food is spot on and amazing. I don't like to go dish by dish but the ravioli I can eat a bowl of. Actually several things I can eat a large bowl of!

Another highlight is wine - super affordable. Had a raveneau Chablis. And a allemand cornas both under $300.. both retail for $150ish so markup is very reasonable for a 2 star place!

After service the server and chefs did shots with us. End of the night so hey! :)

Definitely worth a visit. Just be prepared to wait in a super busy bar in the beginning.

Two words. Panty dropper. Maybe that's a bit crude and I did go with my good friend and no panties were involved - but WHOA! Sometimes you go to a place and you look at the bill at the end of the night and you wonder where your dollars are going and what you could have done instead. Then sometimes you look at the bill and you are wondering for any excuse to come back. This is the latter times ten. 

Part of the vibe is reserving like 2 months out, getting there on time, being taken through robertas and feeling like you are going to a speakeasy then being seated with 10 other guests at the chef's table facing the kitchen of very talented and oddly super hot cooks. When you are there, you are asked if you want the insane wine tasting menu --- by then, how do you refuse. 

Every single plate is curated with enchantment. The problem is that the free-flowing wine by the fourth course you are a little tipsy. They are very good; they have prepared for this well. In the middle of the courses they bring out a fresh loaf of AMAZING bread with salted butter. It's like reinforcements so you can keep eating and drinking. Sooooo good. 

Ingredients are fresh and seasonal. 

Even though it's a total culinary experience they have managed to not make it feel stuffy. 

Orgasmic experience - the plating, the service, the kitchen, the flavors, the wine education -  the whole thing was food porn.

Very special experience here for my boyfriend's birthday. This was my favorite restaurant we dined at in all of NYC and we hit many great spots. This place is not stuffy or overcrowded. It's unassuming and quaint. There are no stuffy dress codes, they want you to come as you are. The service was excellent and ambiance was top tier. The sommelier was delightful, energetic, and friendly. We really enjoyed her! The chef de cuisine was in the kitchen prepping the whole time. You don't see that at all these places. We were blown away by the creativity, quality, and taste. Thank you for a 5 star experience and we cannot wait to come back.

Food is top TOP notch in a comfortable environment, not stuffy at all! Exciting to get to watch the chefs make and plate each dish. 

The wine pairing is a MUST - even if you aren't a wino! The sommelier Missy nails it! Not a single wine or alcohol I didn't appreciate, it all matched splendidly. Everyone serving the meals is fantastic and friendly... 

The food can't really be described so I'll just say that the entire experience is worth every penny!

I thought the food was very good. The pancetta, ravioli, foie gras, pizza bread, beef and lamb stood out. The setting was fuss-free and laid back, I especially liked that. While the food was very good, I had expectations of being blown away and that didn't happen. Having said that, service was on point, food was delicious and overall, a lovely and memorable experience.

I had the most beautiful birthday celebration here. Definitely get the wine pairing as the selection complements every dish wonderfully. the wagyu was the most wonderful thing I ever tasted. I enjoyed every minute of tastebud pleasure and left feeling beautifully tipsy and fully satisfied without being too full.

The space is fun and it feels wonderfully communal to sit with another 10 (or so) people who are eating the same courses simultaneously. But the food is truly blah to awful. It's like a few college friends got together to experiment with sous-vide technique--not very successfully and excluding all other methods of food preparation.  And the bill for 2 was almost $700 including tip. Don't waste your money. With so many wonderful restaurants in the city, don't fall for the hype. I suspect the people who have reviewed this restaurant favorably are simply too insecure to be honest.

There's much to be said about a two-Michelin star restaurant hidden in an iconic pizzeria in Bushwick. Prior to our reservation here I had not heard of Blanca, but was pleasantly surprised when my boyfriend told me he had made reservations a month out for my birthday. A 12-capacity fine dining area inside Roberta's?! I was through the roof.

We had arrived about half an hour early for dinner at 6pm, and headed to the bar at Roberta's for cocktails. Someone then comes to get your party and you are ushered out to the patio and into a hidden dining area. (They let you take the drinks!) In true chef's kitchen fashion, you enter a room with a long dining table and twelve seats - with the kitchen and the staff directly in front of you. We were glad we got seated at the edge, as this was the right balance of being among the crown and being on our own.

I'd read only the best things about this place. A lot of the reviews mentioned how comfortable (and not stuffy) the atmosphere is - check. We were greeted by our friendly sommelier who poured us the best glass of sparkling cider I've ever had. It was so good that we both had another glass later that night. They then explained the options for drinks. I opted for the flight of wine (moderately light to very dry), and my boyfriend the flight of sake. The wine pairing is highly raved about, but I was afraid it would not have been practical as I wouldn't be able to keep up (I was definitely feelin' it, and still had a bit left in one glass of the flight at the end of the night.)

Blanca asks you to come fifteen minutes early. Do not take the request lightly as they do start dinner on time-give or take a couple minutes-without you. Although you are very closely dining with eleven other people and it may seem like a group affair, you do not, at any time, feel like you're at an art gallery tour. The service is very individual to your party, and everything is explained to you by a chef or the other staff. With The Beatles playing in the background, we were off.

You watch the chefs plate each dish very carefully, and it is served to you alongside a short intro of what the dish contains, its origin, etc. The menu varies each night, but you could tell that every single detail of each dish was carefully curated. With a couple sorbet-esque palate cleansers in between, some of my favorites were the sea perch spigarello, the baby corn (people don't eat the leaves apparently but it was too late and I'd already finished it), the paw paw perilla, the tuna matsukate, the beef pluot, the potato bottarga. Oh, and the bread! Each dish, seemingly simple, had very intrinsic flavors. They use a lot of Asian elements in modern Italian cuisine, which was very interesting and enjoyable. The only dish I wasn't super fond of was the last celery granita grape dish - it was a bit too chalk-y for me. Everything else was fantastic. They also brought out a small little platter with nuts and chocolate for my birthday. Was a very sweet touch. With courses as many as Blanca's, I typically tap out on the third to last dish, but we were just the right amount of full this time.

An upscale excursion with a very down to earth vibe. I'd recommend this place to anyone and everyone, especially those who live in the neighborhood. Who would've thought! (This is also a great place to treat yourself and dine alone.) It gives you a solid perspective on just how great food can be anywhere in town.

My boyfriend and I ate a couple of weeks ago for a mini-anniversary.  We booked a month in advance and were super excited to get a seat on a Friday night at one of the most proclaimed restaurants in New York City.  We're big time foodies.  We dine out multiple times a week and are always going to check out different places in different neighborhoods.  We've dined at Roberta's several times and loved the food so to say the least, we were very excited about Blanca.

When we arrived, we were greeted by a lovely woman who told us the hostess would be right with us.  Less than a minute later, we were greeted by a huge smile from the maitre d who I'd been in contact with when setting up the reservation.  She'd remembered every detail of our conversation weeks prior and made us feel so warm and welcome without a hint of that pretentious-trying-too-hard-fake vibe we so often get.  Maybe Bushwick was the place to be after all!

We walked through the lovely garden where young hipsters drank their beer, ate that delicious pizza, and felt somewhat jealous until we arrived into Blanca.  We were shown around, taken to our seats, when we were greeted by the cutest pixie waitress in the world.  Smiles all around, jokes, and again with that warm feeling like we were talking to someone we'd known for years.  

The uni was to die for, loved the corn foie gras.  Let's just say we were in heaven... until after about the fifth or sixth course we started noticing the pace picking up. We were sitting in the last seating, so we didn't understand why the rush. My boyfriend and I noticed the shift in energy. We were now completely distracted by observing this dynamic. The (what seemed like head) chef was running food, pushing people into their seats and clearing plates.  Specifically once as I was still chewing! What was most confusing about this was the amount of times we watched him do all these things when there was a waiter or waitress at the ready quite clearly about to do what he was running to do.  It was almost comical.  Our servers were making us feel comfortable and at ease, but the chef (who for some reason was also trying to be a server that night?) made us, and, quite visibly, the servers, the other chefs, and the entire ambiance uneasy.  Not to mention, rushed.  I don't remember a single dessert.  We didn't have time to process anything.

The rest of the night seemed like a joke. This one guy put me off ever coming back. No reason to spend that amount of money in a weird hostile environment where I can't put my fork down before getting it snatched away from me before I've swallowed my food.

It was such a wonderful experience! Food was delish (obviously since it is a Michelin restaurant). What I love most about the restaurant is that it is so different from any other Michelin restaurant I've been to. Usually they are super stuffy and prim and proper but this seemed to have a more relaxed and casual atmosphere which I thoroughly enjoyed. The meal was great for a tasting menu too since my boyfriend and I left without feeling hungry which we usually do after a tasting menu at Michelin star restaurants (usually their portions are so tiny!) I loved the variety of meat and seafood dishes and the work that goes into each dish (I love uni and we were lucky to have 2 dishes with uni when I went.) The pizza bread was surprisingly delicious too. Great desserts too and the little goody bag which details the different dishes of the meal we had along with their homemade chocolate bar was a nice touch. I also mentioned that my boyfriend and I were there to celebrate our anniversary and they had a little card for us which was nice. Some of the other guests were celebrating their birthdays and the restaurant had noted that as well. That's good service (along with the fact that they were always on top of folding your napkin and getting your seat for you whenever you got up to use the restroom). Also, the setting is very intimate as it's all bar seating for 12 people max I believe. I loved this because it felt like I was sitting at a Chef's Table since it was an open kitchen and we could watch the chef and his team prepare everything for us. He even thanked us at the end of the meal which was a nice personal touch. Also, it felt very cool and speakeasy type because it's in the back of Roberta's pizza and you would never guess that there is a separate restaurant behind the bustling pizza joint. Overall, a great evening and definitely a must-try!

Decent effort, albeit slightly spotty; nonetheless, it was enjoyable!

Food didn't come out until ~6:15pm because one person was late.  People who showed up on time shouldn't be penalized.

A very enjoyable experience with well prepared food. The ingredients aren't as premium as you would expect at that price point though. I would recommend getting the wine pairing because our somm really made our meal wonderful. She was friendly and helpful.

My beef was also pretty chewy and I expected melt-in-your-mouth goodness. The take-home chocolate is a nice touch.

For an expensive, fine dining establishment, I expected better service. I came down with an awful flu and was bedridden only two days prior to my reservation, so I tried to email them to reschedule. I explained the situation and noted that I didn't want to spread the flu to other guests and restaurant staff. They wrote back and told me that I would get charged the full cancellation fee (which is the entire dinner + tax). It was unbelievable. I gathered all my strength to make it to this dinner so I wouldn't lose money and was appalled by the total disregard in putting other people's health at risk.

Never would I have dreamt of eating and enjoying plankton ravioli. This review is long overdue. I apologize for that but this place I will never forget. I am a sucker for locally grown ingredients. When you hear that some of the things you are eating we're grown right there it's even better. I loved the sour beer. Loved the energy of the place. Love how we had to be led thru Roberta's to go to our secret location. Made it that much more special.

It used to be one of my favorite restaurants in new york 2 and a half years ago. I went there 29 times in a year and never got tired of it. Loved the cilantro ice cream so much. But i dont know, something changed within the last year and a half and the foods were not as breathtaking as before. So that was unfortunate. I hope it will get back on track soon. I have hope. Didnt take many pictures here because i was too focus on eating. Hah


***update***
Just went back again last night after a long hiatus from them; and the foods were amazing! The chef has restored my faith. All the courses were well edited and sequenced. The desserts were imaginative, unexpected and playful. Overall, a nice gentle symphony with not too many sour notes. My kind of melody! Haha! Will definitely go back again soon. Maybe next week!
The only thing i will complain is the actual music is very loud. Couldnt barely hear myself talk.

We had made a reservation here for me proposing to my, at the time, girlfriend.  The system accidentally over-booked the reservation and as a result they cancelled our reservation.  After calling, pleading with the restaurant, and multiple follow-ups (the person responsible for reservations was very unresponsive) they were unable to solve the problem; I had to be in contact with the reservation person until day of the proposal.  I was lucky enough to get a reservation with another restaurant of their caliber but was very disappointed that, given the occasion, they were unable to accommodate and so insensitive/unresponsive.  We were hoping to have this venue be a special place for my partner and me, given that we have lived in Brooklyn for so long, and sad they were unable/willing to help us.  Thankful that another restaurant was more accommodating and generous.

Our annual high-roller dinner had us trying out another place in Brooklyn, hidden behind a little pizza shop on a graffiti festooned street.  

I'm going to start with service.  Service.  Service.  Look, I've been to plenty of hoity-toity 3-Michelin star places, and at best the waiters and waitresses at these places can be described as, "Professional", "Polite", and on rare occasions they might even crack *a* joke.  But I've honestly never been to high-class restaurant where I felt like the folks serving me weren't just the staff, but they were friends and we were just chilling at their place enjoying a great meal.  Seriously, on service alone they get to 4-Stars, and the food, well gosh it's just a bonus then innit?  

So, 23 courses, I'm not going to enumerate them all, because unless you go within like 4 weeks of this review, they'll be gone.  There were some rockstars: Polenta-Uni, Mandarin Orange-Caviar, a firecracker ravioli.  There were some dishes that were "Fine", like a pasta with red sauce that felt familar, a room temperature waygu, and a soup that was missing a little something.  They also served an IPA (a drink which I loathe) that was exceedingly good.  

The only MISS for me, no chocolate dessert, or true pastry like thing.  I.  Need.  Chocolate.  But I won't knock them too hard, the desserts that were served were good, I was just having a hankering.  

There were other cool things about this place, the deco was understated, and didn't feel pretentious, the seats were old leather Corvette buckets that were comfy (although my friend opined that there wasn't lumbar, pfft) and the music was top shelf, a communal vinyl collection being spun on a nearby record player.  

There are no shortage of remarkable eateries in NY, Blanca gets the rare distinction of being a place I want to go back to, not because of the food, but because I felt welcome.

Dinner at Blanca last Friday--absolutely the best meal that I have had in years. Reminded me of many memorable meals with Charlie Trotter that I was lucky to enjoy in Chicago, but Blanca takes it to a new level. Each dish was beautifully presented and delicious, the pacing and rhythm of each course was perfectly timed to keep the evening flowing naturally. Fabulous to be able to watch the amazing team put it all together. Fabulous sound track for the meal.
really excellent. worth it.  the space, the staff, the food.  Ive been to lots of places like this and Blanca is one of the best.

Unexpected site and a surprised menu! Had a great time , we have been there twice and we loved it!
Thank You Allegra for making our second visit even better than the first one

Once you fight your way through the chaos outside with the long lines at Roberta's you are transported into a divine and simple space with a counter that seats 13 if I remember correctly. Be ready to embark on a killer experience of 20 courses. From the minute you walk in you know your in Brooklyn as a record player plays the tunes and the servers wear jorts and the vibe is chill. I loved how they wanted to focus on the food and make you feel at home with being super casual and fun. The food was mostly all excellent minus a couple dishes that were a miss in my opinion. I highly recommend this place for the experience and loved the hand written receipt at the end which was a nice touch. My only complaint was that they could not make cocktails as they were beer and wine only even though Roberta's is full bar.

Food was great.

Wine/beer flight was worth it. Also got a pizza on the way out. (These 2 things brought it up to a five-star.)

A 2 Star Michelin restaurant hides inside the pizzeria restaurant. The chef  served us total 17 courses for the entire meal which each dish contains of small amount of food but delicate. They also served us 8 different pairing wines ($95 each person) for each 1 or 2 courses for the entire meal which almost got us drunk when we mixed too much different wine. They only serve 12 diners maximum for 3 hours each time.
Good spot, i went there strictly off reviews. I was pleasantly surprised! Thanks guys

I wanted to love Blanca, I really did. We came at end of August for my fiancè's birthday and made our reservation well in advance, as the 11-person seating fills quickly.  I loved how it was set up-- entering through Roberta's and being escorted through the backyard to the private kitchen/dining counter. I loved the staff-- the sommlier was funny, attentive and witty with interesting pairings (although I could have lived without the sake pairing;) the waiter and waitress never allowing my water glass to go half full, providing commentary on each course and prompt service. I loved the ambiance-- modern open kitchen with Edison bulbs, stark white decor, vinyl spinning an eclectic mix and a giant Marlin on the wall.  It didn't feel pretentious or showy. But sadly, the food fell short. I have to say, overall I enjoyed the tasting menu. The highlight for me was the Roberta's pizza bread, baked fresh before our eyes. I liked the ravioli. I enjoyed the caviar and the custard. But some of the uni courses were a bit too much, especially the pasta with uni.  I also didn't enjoy the foie gras course or the warm tomato course. Frankly, I expected to be blown away by this menu and was sad that the best part was pizza dough. Also, Chef Mirarchi was noticably absent. If you have two seatings nightly for a total of 22 guests, the executive chef should be present. Had I been advised he would not be preparing our meal, I probably would have made a different choice.  

I also have to add that I got violently sick after I returned home, throwing up 21 times and reliving my entire meal well into the next day. I actually thought I was going to die, with no exaggeration, and was moments away from going to the hospital (thank God for Pedialyte!)  Not surprising, the uni and pasta course was the first thing to make a second appearance, completely undigested, (sorry for the graphic details,) leading me to believe something in that dish was bad.  When my fiancè contacted Blanca at 1pm the next day to let them know how sick I got, their response was that "no one else complained." No follow-up. No apologies. No conversation with a manager. Nothing after a very expensive meal that was supposed to be celebratory. I once got sick at Red Robin and their investigation and customer service was better than this Michelin star place.  I am adding a star for the service and staff the night of. But the menu wasn't that spectacular and the fact that I got so sick coupled with the complete disregard of the staff the next day and Chef Mirarchi's absence completely ruined this experience for me. Go to Aska instead.

The restaurant was unwilling to offer me a refund (partial or otherwise) when I became sick and was not able to make the reservation. The restaurant was unresponsive to the email sent but was happy and quick to send me an email for the bill. I will not be going to Blanca anytime soon.

Blanca has been on my list forever, I used to live in Bushwick way back when Blanca first opened but never got around to it. Fast forward 5 years later - my fiancé took me this past weekend for my birthday... and now I'm a huge fan!

Yes, the portions are small, some may say tiny. They're a few bites each at most, and I think by design, to leave you wanting more. If you have a big appetite, eat a big lunch and quit your complaining about the portions being tiny. :) That's exactly what we did and we left happy and full. 

We had 18 courses and each was unique and delicious. Our tasting had two uni courses, some may not have any because the menu always changes. I know some people hate uni but I looveee it so no complaints here, I was in heaven. 

Some of my favorites w/ pics: 

miatake mushrooms with uni powder, Asian pear and a good portion of uni from Hokkaido (stuff of my dreams)

caviar with pine nut purée and a slice of a small citrus fruit (looked like a little tangerine, forgot the name but the combo was so. good.)

aged wagyu beef with fig (this was amazing, also the stuff of my foodie dreams)

uni pasta (with another type of smaller smoother uni)

one bite of a surprisingly tasty spicy pork (nduja) filled ravioli, which fiancé raved about, and was so sad that the portion was one ravioli. He said he could eat a bucketful lol

Anyway, the food was delicious and quite an experience (for example, a goat milk filled ravioli that exploded in my mouth... mmmm). I would definitely go again. The damage was $620 which was including a bottle of $180 champagne (a girl has to have a bottle of champagne on her birthday, right?!). I think all in damage for two was $740ish. You can get a wine pairing for an extra $98 per person but we skipped it because there was no way we were drinking 10+ glasses of wine. #keepinitclassy

KenScale: 8.75/10

After my last visit to Blanca in Bushwick in early 2016, I called the restaurant the epitome of "Brooklyn fine dining" for its unassuming venue inside the Brooklyn hipster institution Roberta's and the free-flowing yet sophisticated dining experience that the kitchen offers so effortlessly. Fast forward to two and a half years later, I was looking for a place to celebrate my wife Jun's birthday and Blanca immediately came to my mind. The dining space with a single counter next to Roberta's outdoor space did not change much from 2016, with a big fish decoration still on the wall. Just like last time, I did not get to see the menu in advance, but I was ready to be surprised anyways, this time with my beloved wife on the side. While It was another phenomenal meal, with several new dishes from my last visit that Jun and I both had a lot to like about.  

The menu format at Blanca has not changed much from 2015 (there is only one single tasting menu); the price, at $198 per person and up from $195 in 2016, has not changed much either. And thankfully, the vibrant creativity of the tasting menu has stayed at a very high level. There is no single culinary influence that defines Blanca's identity, but that is the beauty of the kitchen's approach to the dishes. Sea perch that came out as the third dish was more or less perfectly grilled and together with mustard green underneath was a great way to start the meal. One of our favorite dishes of the night was maitake mushroom accompanied by sea urchin and Asian pear. The smoky feel of the mushroom worked beautifully together with the silky smooth texture of sea urchin and the refreshing Asian pear. Jun is not usually a fan of foie gras, but she was happy to try the one that the kitchen put together with corn surrounding it. The potato that came out looked simple at first, but its texture was quite remarkable, especially with bottarga sauce on the side that gave it a nice bump in flavor. The small pasta series at Blanca has always been one of the most lauded parts of the restaurant's tasting menu, and it did not disappoint either. The agnolotti with goat milk had a rich and complex flavor that was quite addictive, pici with sea urchin was sensational, especially with a spicy kick, and 'nduja ravioli with orange was one delightful bite that Jun and I both enjoyed. One of the more puzzling dishes of the night was a bowl of seasonal vegetables in brodo broth. At first, Jun and I cringed at how sour the broth was; the trick is to have fresh bread (it's actually more like a pizza dough) with butter that came at the same time as this dish. The bread shockingly neutralized the sour taste of the broth and we were able to finish the vegetables with no issue. The meat dishes toward the end of the savory course were also quite memorable. Both the pork and the beef had wonderfully soft and juicy textures that could rival any top-rate steakhouse, and the clever use of aji dulce pepper next to the pork and, to my great surprise because I don't even like that fruit too much, watermelon next to the beef was pure genius. The desserts, from the toasted milk with grappa to marigold with plum in a bowl that resembles a cold soup but with sweet flavor, also displayed thoughtfulness and ingenuity of the kitchen.

Getting a reservation at Blanca (available online up to 28 days in advance, and with at least 7 days prior to cancel) can still be a challenge, and not surprisingly the counter was full during our visit on an early Friday evening. Unlike my last visit, Jun and I did not have a separate drink pairing option; I opted for beer and she did for sake to accompany the meal. I don't remember what the wine list at Blanca looked like last time I visited, but the list today is exclusively natural wines which deterred us from ordering a bottle. I did get a red wine by the glass just to have it for the beef dish, but regretted doing so as it was difficult to overcome its funky taste. The vibe at the dining space still retains that casual Brooklyn vibe which also shows in the diversity of attires from the other diners, from those in T-shirts and jeans to those in fancy blazers and dresses. Nowadays, expensive tasting menu has become out of flavor for its lack of accessibility to the general public and the elitist image it seemingly cultivates, but I find Blanca to be so refreshing in that sense; it shows that serious cooking can still be enjoyed without feeling like the one percent. Blacna, for that matter, should be considered one of the most influential restaurants in NYC.

Hands down, one of the best dining experiences we have had, comparing it to the usual suspects like Per Se, Jean Georges, Le Bernardin, Daniel etc. 
Spectacular service.. they accommodated every dietary restriction without skipping a beat. Also, each of their wines are meticulously sourced with the most uniquely designed labels.Every course superseded the previous one. DON'T MISS OUT!!!

Definitely something I have never tried before. Blanca is 2 Michelin-Star fine dining experience located inside and through the Roberta restaurant. The restaurant was beautiful! I love the clean aesthetics: open kitchen, vinyl music, plant walls and wood structures.

I had no idea what to expect, but this definitely blew my mind. Every course is a bite-size intricately-constructed dish.

Some favorites of the night:
Maitake mushrooms with Maine sea urchin - delicious pairing of creamy uni with perfectly crisp and grilled mushrooms. 
Hokkaido uni with pici - Super flavorful (with a kick) pasta dish paired with creamy uni and a perfect amount of breadcrumbs. I wish i can eat this all day.
Seasonal vegetables with a tangy broth served with a side of pizza dough bread - This was heaven in a bowl. I actually enjoyed each of the veggies that was presented- it seemed like each of them had a different flavor and the broth was so intense. I loved dipping the bread into the broth. I'm still drooling thinking about it.
120 day dry-aged wagyu - Dry aged? Wagyu? It's like heaven in your mouth. The cut was so melty, soft and juicy.

Unique:
Caviar and parsnip - Very unique flavor combo, salty and refreshing.
Andouille sausage ravioli - Melty filling with a good amount of spice.
Habanada ice cream - I normally can't eat spicy, so I never tried habaneros before. Finally get to taste what it was like without the heat. It was really interesting flavor. 

They also gave us goodie bags with the menu and home-made Portuguese tarts.

EASILY the BEST meal I had in 2018, and possibly one of the top 5 meals I've had ever!

Came here with 3 other friends for a farewell dinner for a dear friend - so glad we were able to enjoy this together. Reservations are available 30 days ahead, so be sure to click that button at midnight! They are located hidden behind Roberta's, and the vibe is completely different - sleek, modern, minimalistic, aka really cool! Their tasting menu is $198pp, and you have the option of adding on a wine pairing as well. The sommelier was pretty great, so I thought it was a pretty worthy splurge (it's not unlimited glasses like it was at brooklyn fare when it was still in brooklyn though!).

We had a total of 18 dishes - I felt like it was a great variety of different cuisines, but nothing clashed with one another. The dishes were very well thought out, fine dining without being pretentious! Standout dishes for me were the corn foie gras, goat milk agnolotti, fresh bread, sea urchin pici, and all the fish dishes. The portuguese tart they let you take away with you is the perfect gift/ending to the meal, wish we could actually buy those!

Hopefully i'll get another blanca meal in 2019!!!

Blanca is my favourite fine dining place in NYC. The atmosphere is casual but intimate, and the italian/japanese fusion omakase style eating is amazing. There are usually a few courses (like the chorizo ravioli) that are unforgettable and it's somewhere I would highly recommend for a special occasion.

We came here for my wife's birthday. For the price, I thought it was atrocious. The pasta courses are good; we loved the andouille ravioli. The duck and waygu course was solid as well. The desserts were the most disgusting things I've ever eaten for a dessert at this price point. We had some weird habanero sorbet and then some pistachio coconut soup. It was memorable for how bad it was.  For our goodbye bag they handed us some fruitcake which they said was really good. I tried it and hated it so much I left it at the restaurant. I think next time, I'll just eat pizza at Roberta's.

Excellent. Brought my boyfriend for his birthday. Was concerned as he doesn't love uni and I read in the reviews that uni is a featured item in some of the courses. Overall, I'd still say it was worth it! (He says he does not sign off on this review if it's any more than 3.5 stars, I disagree).

We waited at Roberta's bar for 5-10 minutes (got there early) before we were lead through the back to the actual Blanca space. It was beautiful, simple with 12 seats. I think everyone there opted for the wine pairing.

Each dish was well constructed and it was entertaining getting to watch the chefs cook. Dinner was around 1.5 hours- everything was perfectly timed with the dishes and wine and everything ran very smoothly. Our favorites were the caviar, the pancetta was actually out of this world (I'll never be able to eat any other pancetta again), duck, wagyu beef, and goats milk agnolotti that literally melted in your mouth. I'd definitely recommend this place for a cool experience / special occasion (a little of the same type of attention to detail / unusual dishes / tightly run dinner like Blue Hill at Stone Barns but not as mind blowing) but no need to come more than once.

As other reviewers have mentioned as well, it's not an overwhelming amount of food so you may leave hungry. Yes, we did try and guess when dinner would be over, look up Roberta's take out menu, call Roberta's from where we were seated to place an order and picked it up for when we got home. And yes, we may be gluttonous and over-the-top for food, but we ate that whole pizza and it was worth it!

I have never been here, only to Roberta's, however I have to agree with Samantha A. I went to their pop up restaurant at Frieze Art Fair, Foul Witch and experiences the worst service in NYC. Out of the 3 courses we ordered only two made it to the table. We were still charged a 22% gratuity. When we refused to pay for service that did not hold up to a 22% standard, the manager was extrémalo rude to us claiming that "That is the price of eating in NYC and at an art fair." When we still refused to pay the gratuity, the manager threatened to call the cops and even cursed at us. It was quite an expensive meal $85+, the food quality was sub-par, and not to mention the service was TERRIBLE.  I was quite surprised of the treatment considering they are part of a two star Michelin Restaurant. Having read that I am not the first one to get bad customer service from the staff I do not recommend the experience, definitely not for the price you pay.

Can't even explain how special this meal was. From the wine pairing (sake/sours/sparkling wines of all varieties), to the beautiful, delectable dishes, to the incredible music playing via record player - this place is pure magic. Truly one of a kind.
Wow.

On the train heading to Manhattan from Bushwick. It almost sounds like a joke but I had a 2 star Michelin experience at a counter behind the tiki bar of a renowned Bushwick pizza place. Blanca is special. It's fun, quirky and delicious. 16 small courses ranged from ice cold citrus sections with tiny balls (the size of caviar) burst with a lime punch. And yes there was caviar, with a fresh liquidy cheese--don't judge, just enjoy. Friendly and unpretentious--I also know where all my old vinyl went. Great music. And get the pairings-cider, ale, sake and vino. Perfectly nuanced. Gracias Blanca.

Do you know how there's a current trend of high fashion street wear? Blanca is like the food equivalent, but in a good way. I'm glad a place like this exists in the world and what better place for it to exist than Brooklyn.

Love this very brooklyn dining experience. Hidden in the pop pizza place with graffiti on the street outside. Very casually wore staff. Loud hipster music. Not special ingredients but cook them into a different level. First time saw a plate of potato as one course, and first time eating with hands at a non-sushi Michelin restaurant. 

Food is delicious too! We had 18 courses, and I can pretty much remember all the courses without looking at the photos, which is quite rare. Lol
My favorites: 
Barbecue ribs. This is the best barbecue I've ever had!! The chef cooked it for at least 30 mins, on and the off the rack. Perfect seasoning, well balance of sweet and savory. LOVE It!
All the pasta dish. Never had that much pasta dishes in a fine dining menu, but they are all really good! The sauce, the texture of the pasta. Would love to have a plate of them! 

Drawbacks: we left feeling like we can have another slice of the pizza outside, and I don't have a big appetite. Usually I would be extremely full after the fine dining meal. Well, maybe that's the point of restaurant being in the pizza place? 
The desserts were very simple too, and kind of repetitive. Just many, many sorbets. 
There were only two protein courses in the 18 courses menu. Although the short ribs were really good, feeling like we could have one more protein.

I took my man for his birthday and we both had a blast ! This was our second chefs table and we really enjoyed it ! Staff was phenomenal and food was delicious . We also did the wine pairing was definitely worth it and everyone should do it ! 
The ambiance was incredible ! Vinyl records playing while you eat in these comfortable chairs and explosion of food in your mouth ! WORTH EVERY PENNY!! Highly recommend

Great tasting menu and one of a kind experience, felt like we were invited to eat at a secret location.

It is tucked away in the back of a pizzaria, but just walk through the main entrance and ask the hostess and they are more than willing to walk you over.

My wife and I went to Blanca to celebrate our anniversary and it was an amazing experience. With a limited seating per night, we were able to have an intimate dining set fused decadent and delicious food. It's not a surprise Blanca is Michelin star rated :)

The whole dining experience ran about 2-3 hours and the dress code was dressy casual, very enjoyable and comfortable at the same time.

Every dish was presented expertly with an intricate description and story. Our favorite is by far the ribs!

Highly recommend and we will definitely be back!

An amazing restaurant with a lovely crew and a stellar tasting menu. Worth a trip from wherever you are in New York, Blanca will deliver the perfect mix of exquisite food and cool ambience, culinary rigor and sans souci feel (as should be in any dining establishment of caliber).  The space in itself is a pure work of art, well lit and attentively decorated with plants, a vinyl collection and a very spacious and spotless kitchen (probably the biggest you will see in a Michelin starred restaurant).  My favorites include the caviar, the cavatelli, the 'Nduja ravioli, the fresh bread and butter, sunflower and habanada.  Every member of the staff is in a great mood and always looking after the guests without placing them under the scrutiny.  The chef was present and harmoniously conducted, overlooked and participated in the preparation and plating of each dish.  I really appreciated the relaxed atmosphere.  A pure joy of dining and a pleasure to the eyes:  Blanca deserves three stars and more.  Such a delight to the palate and the spirit.  I can't wait to go back.

Very special dinner atmosphere, but tbh still left starving! Would recommend as a fun night out to celebrate, some truly incredible bites, but lost out on a rave review feeling as after 3 hours all we wanted was pizza or anything substantial. Not new to tasting menus and aware of the small size portions, but for $750 for 2 (dinner, wine pairing) I'd hope I wasn't leaving and rushing home to get a frozen pizza in the oven. :)

Well hello you naughty little secret at the back of Roberta's !


If you want to a do a tasting menu without the foo foo white table clothes and romance this is the place. 

Date night or a splurge with a friend this place of amazing. 

I highly recommend the wine pairing !
One of the best meal experiences of my life. The drink pairing was so unique and interesting - definitely recommend it.

Definitely one of the best Michelin restaurants in the greater New York area.  It is a little hard to find at first and the area is trendy but you wouldn't think that it would have such an outstanding fine dining experience.

Glad Blanca reopened and finally get to try.
Interesting approach but not sure how I feel about it. It's very "internationally" inspired. Some random thoughts during the meal -

Crab Empanada is the most generous in size dish that I've seen at any tasting menu joint.

Tortilla Bread's texture was very interesting. The crust is much thicker and flakier than usual bread, I enjoyed a lot.

Uni soaked in a bed of leche de tigre, and drizzled with hot sesame oil - not exactly sure how this creation came from but feel like it's random and didn't blend well, uni's flavor was lost.

Seaweed Tortelli was tasty but couldn't taste seaweed.

Korean Spinach suddenly got served?

Feel like traveled the world in this meal but not in a cohesive way. Appreciate the creativity behind it though!

I came in with admittedly high expectations, but my friends and I all rated Blanca a 5 or 6 out of 10.  Good service made up for somewhat uninspiring food.  

The first course of citrus and fermented brussels sprouts was delicious, as was the crab empanada.  The other seafood courses, including an uni ceviche, were not memorable. 

Surprisingly, the pasta courses were several notches below what you might have somewhere like Misi; the flavors were delicate to the cusp of blandness and would have benefited from a stronge point of view.  

Overall, the meal felt incohesive and inconsistent.  If I was being taken on a journey, I lost the plot.  While I'm glad I was able to experience this menu, there are many other similar caliber restaurants I would return to first.

This was very good, albeit quite pricey. All the dishes were very flavorful and thoughtfully prepared. Was a little nervous I wasn't going to get enough to eat but was more than sated by the end of the meal, which lasted close to 3 hours. While they have an optional wine pairing, we brought our own bottle. The corkage is a little steep and probably only worth it if you have a great bottle to enjoy with the excellent food. Nice space and comfortable chairs at the bar. The service, while very professional and attentive, seemed a little cold at times. Whatever. Not there to make friends.

Blanca excludes people with Jewish dietary restrictions. I wanted to take my fiance to Blanca for her birthday. I made the reservation weeks in advance. A few days before, Blanca emailed and said they would not accommodate Kosher dietary restrictions--i.e., pork or shellfish. Absolutely bizarre in this day and age. Blanca also said they would cancel our reservation "without penalty as a one time courtesy." There's nothing courteous about refusing to accommodate a widely held religious dietary restriction. Restaurants should be open and welcoming. Not whatever this is.

Went there Thursday night with a friend. The food, the service, and the ambiance were all excellent. Can't speak more highly of this restaurant. Smaller, more intimate space with an open kitchen. Come hungry because there's food a plenty here. Just eat whatever they put in front of you, and you will be happy. Took us a while to get the reservation but it was very worth it.

I can't imagine how disappointed the original owners must be - this is the coldest experience from top to bottom. It is clear the staff fears chef Victoria. I watched her repeat the same story before the bread course to all the diners with not a single word changed from person to person. It seemed painful for her to even offer a smile. So cold and robotic - which is exactly like the restaurant itself. Blanca used to be a culmination of sorts. You would go to Roberta's for the best pizza, pasta, charcuterie, cheese, cocktails, craft beer, natural wine etc. eventually you would make your way to Blanca for something really special. Now they are just mailing in some sort of strange mash up of cuisines to pay off the private equity investors. The sommelier couldn't tell you the difference between a white and a red. It's hard to express how disappointing this is. I will just feel bad for some time to know how far this place has fallen. I hate to think people save up for this experience. I hate to think tourists think this is what Brooklyn has to offer.

I'm so bummed to only give 2 stars. What was outstanding was the ambiance, experience, and staff. It's a long, experimental meal. There are only a few seats around an open kitchen, so you get to watch the staff cooking, plating, and serving. 

However, I found the food very lackluster, especially against other Michelin restaurants of similar prices. There were a few dishes that I liked, but most I found incredibly muted if not unpleasant. For example, there was an oyster with a sauce and a candied tuile on top. They suggested you cracked the tuile and take bites with a bit of everything...then it just tasted like there was a shard of sugar sweet candy on my oyster. Not good, very bizarre. At these prices, I can't chance coming back for a menu that underwhelming.

Blanca. An exceptional culinary experience. Blanca is under the skilled direction of Chef Victoria Blamey who constructs a bold menu that is seafood-centric and infuses new age and Chilean elements that tantalize and invigorate. Blanca features six chefs preparing an 18-course tasting menu that is served out over a three-hour culinary excursion. The flavors are intense and sophisticated through the pairing of seemingly contrary ingredients: pasta with lavender and celery foam, crab empanadas with wakame, crab with sauerkraut.

The food is thought provoking and challenges the norms of fine dining. But it works. Very well, in fact.

Blanca is located at the back of Roberta's, a graffiti decorated pizzeria and getting to the door is an Indiana Jones-esque trek. The decor is Japanese minimalist; its most notable feature being the large tuna head on the wall.

Blanca is well worth the more than $300 per head price. But be warned: reservations are at least two months out so you need to be either very well organized or know someone.

Excellent dining experience at Blanca. Each course had unique flavors and ingredients - while the classics like the empanada and bread we knew would be top notch, we really enjoyed the full menu. One of the more notable dishes for me was the swiss chard with white chocolate sesame, and my partner enjoyed the winter ceviche (i believe it had surf clams in it). 

We tried 6 different wines with the pairing and not surprisingly, it enhanced each dish! My favorite wine was the Beaujolais, though I appreciated they also included more local specialties from Kato Sake Works and Springs Brewing.

Service was fantastic. They noticed the little details (there was a lefty dining at the table, and they ensured cutlery was set on the left) and explained the dishes and ingredients well. 

Lovely experience, perfect for a celebratory occasion!

I had dinner there and lost my wallet (either at restaurant or my way home). There is NO way to contact them by phone. I tried calling multiple times and no one is ever available. Also i sent 2 emails and they DO NOT RESPOND!!. Super annoying.

Deceptively simple dishes, but often felt like everything could have had something.. more. Had a mussel and cabbage dish that seemed literally just that with a little broth and some green garlic puree. I watched a couple take a bite of it then both shrug their shoulders LOL. Several dishes caused responses like that. Another one was the plantain stuffed into a sweet potato topped with a garlic chip and chili oil on top of tahini. It was good, but nothing made me excited to return. Highlight of the meal for me was the pawpaw sorbet. 

I will say I didn't leave feeling overly full or gross like I do after some tastings that have a ton of butter based sauces. I enjoyed having dishes I haven't had before like the dense pork belly bread and the Chilean seaweed relish. Service was super fun. Thought the staff were great, made me laugh a few times.

Overall: for the price, I think I was expecting more. I need to come back and try another menu.

Not sure this version of the restaurant is salvageable. Missing the old Blanca. A few good courses, namely the monkfish liver and the bonito. The crab empanada is maybe supposed to be fun but feels like overpaying for mediocre street food, and the bread course is just burnt. Even the dry-aged steak fell flat. Good service and staff so pains me to write this, but wishing we hadn't gone back to try it again.
